c1bdb86c135f3c96: KUALA LUMPUR: Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has reminded police personnel to maintain discipline and respect senior officers to preserve the force's strength and harmony.
Khalid said respect for senior officers appeared to be declining, raising concerns that this could weaken the force and undermine its standing among other government agencies.

"We know that observing the proper chain of command is essential. We must show respect to the seniors," he said at the IGP's monthly gathering organised by the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department at Bukit Aman today.

He reminded personnel to maintain the discipline instilled during training throughout their service, adding that being reprimanded should not be viewed negatively, but taken as an opportunity to improve.
"Being corrected is not a wrongdoing in itself, but should serve as a lesson to help personnel recognise that a mistake has been made.

"We should not view being reprimanded as a sign of weakness. We should ensure criticisms are constructive and help build character, enabling us to fulfil our duties and responsibilities with greater competence, discipline, and integrity," he said.
Khalid said personnel must respect one another, accept feedback, and acknowledge that they are not always right, while fostering cooperation and solidarity within the force.

Meanwhile, he said the police will celebrate Integrity Day on Nov 11 under the theme "Integriti dan Organisasi Bukan Pilihan Tetapi Kewajipan" (Integrity and Organisation: Not a Choice, but an Obligation).
He added that the celebration will honour 35 police personnel who rejected bribes in the line of duty, recognising them as role models for their colleagues.

9e02525728baf1c4: The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) has been entrusted with stewardship of four additional AI projects in the hope of broadening the set of vendor-neutral tools for making AI agents.

The AAIF was founded in December 2025 under the auspices of the Linux Foundation as a vendor-neutral organization for the benefit of AI companies more interested in riding a tide that lifts all boats than making waves.
It launched with three projects under its supervision: Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, and AGENTS.md. With the four new adoptees, there are now 10 projects sheltering under the AAIF's wings.
The donor organizations – Alibaba, Anthropic, Hugging Face, and OpenAI – have handed over control of OpenSandbox, Agent Skills, OpenEnv, and Open Responses respectively.

Each of these projects provides functions that developers of AI agents – which typically combine models, tools, and a task loop – may find helpful. And having a more or less agreed-upon blueprint for implementation tends to make deployment easier and more predictable, at least until your AI agent unexpectedly ransacks some third-party organization.

OpenSandbox provides a way to constrain or sandbox the capabilities of AI agents using various client SDKs, tools, protocols, lifecycle hooks, container runtimes, and assorted in-sandbox execution components.
Agent Skills outlines a format for text descriptions that guide AI agents through specified tasks more effectively. It provides context that helps agents accomplish their goals.
"We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral," said Anthropic, an AAIF co-founder, in a blog post.
OpenEnv offers a containerized service for creating reinforcement learning environments that can be built without much trouble, can interoperate, and can scale to meet demanding testing.

And Open Responses is an open API specification for building LLM interfaces that can work with different model providers. It standardizes common request and response formats, streaming events, and tool invocation patterns.

The AAIF's nurturing of these technical specs has attracted considerable interest from companies convinced that there's a future in AI agents. The organization has surpassed 300 members in less than a year, with 60 coming on board this quarter, including Ant Group, Gates Foundation, MongoDB, Nutanix, Royal Bank of Canada, Vercel, and Vultr as Gold Members.

This enthusiastic (or credulous) embrace of AI agents may be a bit too rapid for some industries. Axios is reporting that US banks have become concerned that AI agents are interacting with customer accounts without bank authorization (though not necessarily without customer authorization). ®

98d5a01a9e98556e: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's poorest households are left with just 1.8 per cent of gross income after consumption expenses in 2024, down sharply from 10.8 per cent in 2019, as rising spending eroded their financial buffers.

Median monthly household expenditure reached RM4,758 in 2024, growing at an annualised rate of 5.3 per cent from 2022 compared with 5.1 per cent annual growth in median household income to RM7,017, according to Khazanah Research Institute (KRI).
KRI, in its "From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026" report, said expenditure among the bottom 10 per cent of households by income rose 21.3 per cent between 2019 and 2024.
Across the bottom 70 per cent of households, spending increased by more than 15 per cent over the same period, while expenditure among the top 10 per cent barely changed.
The shrinking financial buffer leaves poorer households with less capacity to absorb further increases in living costs or build savings.
KRI noted that the residual income measure excludes other outgoings, including taxes, loan repayments and transfers to other households, which would further reduce the amount available for savings.
Health and lifestyle trends also add to household pressures. Malaysian households spent an average of RM902.70 a month eating out in 2024, exceeding the RM875.80 spent on food at home.
Meanwhile, 54.4 per cent of Malaysian adults were overweight or obese in 2023, while physical activity declined between 2019 and 2023, the report found.
KRI said household wellbeing must be assessed beyond income and expenditure, taking into account health and other factors that affect living standards.
cdc78f5cbf9a8b47: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the government's ban on Waze among civil servants, but maintained that national security must take precedence over convenience.
He acknowledged that the decision had drawn criticism, with some questioning why the government had acted so quickly.
However, Anwar said the risks identified by the government were serious enough to warrant immediate action.
"I know I have been criticised and condemned for being hasty.

"If this causes some inconvenience, I apologise. But to me, national security is more important," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Al-Mustaqim in Taman Nirwana, Ampang, today.

He said he had ordered checks into Waze's operations and legal arrangements, which he said confirmed that the navigation application was linked to Israel and that its terms were governed by Israeli law.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he understood complaints about the limitations of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu.
He maintained that the inconvenience was a price worth paying to protect sensitive information.
"It is better to be safe than to hand over confidential state information, your personal information and the country's information to Israel.
"That is what matters to us," he said.
He also urged Malaysians to understand the government's position, particularly given Malaysia's strong opposition to Israel.
Anwar said the government would continue examining alternative navigation applications while improvements were made to existing local options.

On Wednesday, the government announced a ban on the use of Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's status as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
The government said the move was necessary to prevent potential threats to national security and protect sensitive information.
Waze has denied allegations that it collects sensitive government information or allows third parties to exploit users' personal data.
The company described the allegations as untrue and maintained that it operates under strict privacy policies and complies with applicable data protection standards.
The government has also encouraged the use of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA).
However, TuJu has faced complaints over technical shortcomings, prompting the MHA to announce improvements to its navigation function.

76fcdbf1d95e3135: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's household wellbeing has improved across several measures, but sharp regional income disparities and uneven access to higher-paying jobs continue to shape living standards, Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) said.

Median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, rising at an annual rate of 5.1 per cent from 2022, while the labour force participation rate increased to 70.6 per cent from 69.3 per cent in 2022 and 68.7 per cent in 2019.
The Malaysia Happiness Index also rose to 7.60 in 2024 from 6.48 in 2021, said KRi in its "From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026" report today.
The Malaysian Wellbeing Index showed that economic and social wellbeing had generally improved since 2000.
However, the gains remain uneven geographically, with economic activity and higher-paying jobs concentrated in urban centres, particularly Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, according to KRI.
In 2024, median monthly wages stood at RM2,851 in urban areas, against RM1,698 in rural areas. Rural median household income was just 56.4 per cent of the urban level.
Of Malaysia's 166 districts, 111 recorded poverty rates above the national rate of 5.1 per cent in 2024, highlighting persistent disparities in economic opportunities.

Access to basic services has improved considerably. In 2024, 97.8 per cent of households were within 5km of a public health facility, while 98.7 per cent were within 5km of a primary school and 95.9 per cent within 5km of a secondary school.
Nearly all households also had access to treated piped water, electricity and telecommunications.
KRI cautioned that higher incomes and access to infrastructure alone do not guarantee better wellbeing. Age, gender and employment conditions also matter.
Older households tend to have lower incomes and greater health risks, while women continue to face lower labour force participation and a persistent wage gap.
Informal workers, particularly in rural areas, also face greater job insecurity and weaker access to employment-related protections.
The report further warned that Malaysia's dependence on a limited number of countries for food imports exposes households to potential supply disruptions and price shocks.
Such increases would weigh more heavily on lower-income households, which spend a larger share of their budgets on food.
0af7392926511a85: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian households are now spending more on eating out than on groceries to prepare meals at home, according to a new report by the Khazanah Research Institute (KRI).
The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, found that Malaysian households spent an average of RM902.70 a month on eating out, compared with RM875.80 on groceries.

Eating out accounted for 16.2 per cent of total household spending, up from 12.6 per cent in 2016, and was the single biggest driver of higher household expenditure between 2022 and 2024, rising by RM78.20.

According to the report, the increase in food spending was more pronounced among the bottom 80 per cent of households, whose average food expenditure rose by nearly 1.5 times cumulatively between 2019 and 2024.
“For the top 20 per cent (of households), the increase (in food expenditure) was less than 1.3 times,” it said.

The shift in lifestyle has also contributed to concerns over non-communicable diseases, with several Malaysian states recording higher prevalence of diabetes, hypertension and high cholesterol than the national averages in 2023, the report said.
Diabetes was among the top five causes of death in most states between 2022 and 2024, it added.
More than half of Malaysian adults (54.4 per cent) were also above the healthy weight range in 2023, while physical activity declined in urban areas between 2019 and 2023, the report said.
53b30b4f1096d1d0: JAKARTA: Bank Indonesia (BI) on Friday pushed back against criticism by some in the market that its latest policy package was confusing, saying the measures were aimed at improving how its decisions flow through to the broader economy.

The central bank this week kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, raised the overnight deposit facility rate, announced cuts to banks' reserve requirement ratio (RRR) and offered more foreign exchange hedging discounts, in a policy mix that some economists described as "perplexing", "confusing" or "complex".
"This is BI's strategy to harmonise and synchronise our policy rate with our monetary operations strategy," Firman Mochtar, BI's head of economic and monetary policy, told a press conference.
Firman said the higher deposit facility rate restored a symmetrical interest-rate corridor, bringing both the deposit and lending facility rates to 75 basis points from the benchmark rate.
BI had previously maintained a wider 100-basis-point gap between the benchmark and deposit rates because of government fund placements in commercial banks, he said.

He was referring to the government's controversial decision to move excess cash from BI to state-controlled banks to increase banking liquidity. Following a change in leadership at the finance ministry, some of the funds have been withdrawn.
Going forward, it would be better to harmonise the policy rate corridor with BI's monetary targets, Firman said.
He added that the corridor adjustment was consistent with the central bank's planned reserve-requirement cuts.
BI has briefed market participants on the changes, he said.

The central bank plans to cut reserve requirements by a cumulative 200 basis points by December. However, changes to its liquidity incentive scheme mean the effective reserve ratio will fall to about two per cent, roughly 100 basis points below its previous level.

"The additional liquidity is not massive. We have calculated and it's consistent with the BI rate and economic activities," Firman said, estimating an increase of 90 trillion rupiah (US$4.98 billion) in liquidity.
Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, BI's head of monetary management, said the central bank also wants banks to favour shorter-dated instruments over parking excess funds in its rupiah securities, known as SRBI.

BI had previously raised interest rates on SRBI to attract foreign capital inflows. However, Erwin said BI has reduced the level of outstanding SRBI from 1,096 trillion rupiah in July to below 950 trillion rupiah now.

Bank of America economists initially labelled BI's policy mix as "hold, hike and cut all at once" and "perplexing". They later said in a note the measures were less contradictory than they first appeared.
"The RRR cuts do not necessarily signal a reduced willingness to hike policy rate if needed, in our view," they wrote.
26d7f8fb98273987: LONDON, Oct 23 — Dame Judi Dench, one of Britain’s most celebrated actors, says her failing eyesight has taken her off the stage and away from reading.
The Oscar-winning actress, 91, was diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in 2012, and it has since made it incredibly difficult for her to even recognise faces.
“I can’t be on stage. I can’t do a play anymore. I can’t do a film anymore. I can’t read anymore,” she said in an interview on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme.
Her sight loss has increasingly affected her work, with Dench previously speaking about struggling to see on film sets and having difficulty learning scripts.
It also leads to awkward moments, as she sometimes approaches the wrong people and gives them “an almost hug” before realising her mistake.
On the subject of ageing, she was brisk, saying there was “nothing to say for it at all” and that she did not think about it too much.
Even so, she has kept up public appearances and spoken openly about adapting to deteriorating vision, saying that “the radio has always been important to me”.
Dench’s career spans more than seven decades across theatre, television and film.
She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress in 1999 for playing Queen Elizabeth I in Shakespeare in Love.
She also became internationally known as M, James Bond’s boss, making her debut as the first woman to play the role in GoldenEye in 1995.
During the interview, she recalled being invited to lunch by former MI6 chief Sir David Spedding, which she described as “very exciting”.
When she asked where her driver should drop her off, she was told a car would be sent to pick her up instead.
She arrived about 20 minutes late after that driver struggled to find her house.
She said she apologised for being late because the driver could not find her home, adding: “I loved it.”
Asked if she had any views on who should play the next Bond, she simply replied “no”.
Dench also recalled meeting American actor Sidney Poitier, who became the first black man to win the Academy Award for Best Actor in 1964.
She was appearing in Amy’s View in New York when Poitier came backstage after a performance.
Director Richard Eyre was in her dressing room giving her notes when there was a knock at the door.
Dench said she felt as if she were in a wind tunnel when Poitier walked in, calling it “thrilling”.
Asked what she said to him, she admitted it was “not much, a bit of an open mouth”, adding that he was “so charming” and “very tall”.
The conversation then turned to her love of Shakespeare, which she traced to watching her brother play King Duncan in Macbeth when she was nine.
She recalled thinking “oh my God, this is for me” when he walked on and asked, “What bloody man is that?”
She also admitted to being “besotted” by Shakespeare’s sonnets, saying: “I just love them.”
She said it was the rhythm of them, “the rhythm of your heart”, and the way he so simply sums up how any of us feel about “anything”.
57335f07753017f3: KUALA LUMPUR: Comfort Gloves Bhd has reached an agreement with the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) to settle a two-year tax dispute involving its subsidiaries for RM8.3 million, a fraction of the original amount.

In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the glove manufacturer said its subsidiaries, Comfort Rubber Gloves Industries Sdn Bhd (CRGI) and Gallant Quality Sdn Bhd (GQ), reached the agreement on Oct 22, subject to the finalisation of settlement documentation.
"The settlement is not expected to have any material financial impact on the group, as the settlement amount has been provided for in CRGI and GQ's financial statements," it said.
Upon finalisation of the documentation, the subsidiaries will discontinue all legal proceedings over the disputed tax assessments, bringing the matter to a full and final resolution.
The dispute began in April 2024 when both subsidiaries initiated legal proceedings against the IRB over additional tax assessments totalling RM99.3 million.

The assessments arose from the IRB's reassessment of the tax basis period following Comfort Gloves' change of financial year-end to Dec 31, 2021, despite the company having previously obtained the necessary approval.
At 2.40pm, Comfort Gloves' shares were up half a sen, or 3.03 per cent, at 17 sen, valuing the company at RM99.1 million.
fbca40d6c8d911bc: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Chinese stars Cheng Lei and Xu Ruohan’s new Republican-era romance drama The Lament of Autumn has climbed to No. 1 on iQiyi Malaysia’s Hot Dramas chart within its first week, with a rating of 9.8.

Viewers welcomed the drama’s arrival on the platform, expressing excitement about Cheng’s character, Yu Chang Xuan.
The actor, who serves as iQiyi International’s global ambassador, visited Kuala Lumpur in September as part of the Starship programme, where he met local fans.
During the event, he took part in games, learned popular Malay phrases, showcased his photography skills and read fans’ letters on stage.

In The Lament of Autumn, Cheng as Yu is the fifth young master of the Yu family, presenting himself as a charming playboy but also a calculating strategist navigating the turmoil of warlord-era China.
The drama follows Ye Ping Jun, played by Xu, a student who takes a job at a meeting house in western Hunan to pay for her mother’s medical treatment.
On her first day, Ping Jun becomes entangled in an assassination attempt involving Yu and is wrongly suspected of involvement.
Refusing to accept the accusations, she enters into a 10-day pact with him to investigate the case and clear her name.
As they work together, Yu grows closer to her, though his pursuit is complicated by hidden intentions.
What follows is a tale of mystery, hidden secrets, and a gradual romance unfolding amid the chaos of warlord-era China.
The Lament of Autumn premiered on October 12, with 20 of its 38 episodes now out.
3fb44f6a6dd48b83: TEMERLOH: Four men pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to committing armed gang robbery involving East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) cables on Oct 9.
S. Ravindran, 22; A. Suriya Prakash, 21; M. Tenish, 22; and L. Rumes, 34, entered their pleas after the charge was read jointly before judge Ahmad Rizki Abdul Jalil.
According to the charge, the four allegedly committed gang robbery involving cables and staging supports belonging to the ECRL project, worth an estimated RM10,000, while armed with a rusty parang.
The offence was allegedly committed at an ECRL project store in Sri Tualang, Temerloh, at 10.45pm on Oct 9.

The charge was framed under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery and robbery with a dangerous weapon, which carry a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Khairunnisa Zaffar prosecuted, while all four accused were represented by M. Varunchelvam.
Ahmad Rizki fixed bail at RM15,000 with one surety for each accused and set Dec 3 for mention.
The accused were among 17 men arrested earlier this month on suspicion of belonging to four gangs linked to robberies and cable theft involving the ECRL project and Telekom Malaysia in Temerloh.
7d6881bcda4f224e: PETALING JAYA, Oct 23 — Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has instructed his lawyers to begin defamation proceedings against Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan over corruption allegations the latter made against him yesterday.
In a statement today, Rafizi said he had handed the video and transcript of Ramanan’s press conference to his legal team.
“They believe there are strong grounds to bring a lawsuit against R. Ramanan, as his statements at the press conference crossed the boundaries set by the country’s defamation laws,” he said.
Rafizi said Ramanan, who is also PKR vice-president, had made various allegations against him at the press conference, including accusing him of involvement in corruption.
Rafizi had previously named Ramanan as the PKR MP who allegedly accepted a RM9.5 million bribe to settle a case involving what he described as the “corporate mafia”.

He said yesterday’s press conference confirmed that Ramanan had never filed a lawsuit over that claim, and that the minister had reiterated he would not do so, despite earlier threatening to sue anyone who implicated him.
“If R. Ramanan refuses to sue me, his press conference yesterday has now opened the way for me to take him to court over the allegations he made against me,” Rafizi said.
He added that the legal action was also appropriate as Ramanan continued to evade several corruption allegations concerning him.
Rafizi also said Ramanan’s press conference showed that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement in Parliament this week, which claimed Ramanan had initiated court proceedings, was untrue.
He said he would leave it to MPs to take the next step of referring Anwar to Parliament’s Rights and Privileges Committee.
a102254dac337c35: SEPANG: Two Chinese citizens were jailed for six months each by the magistrate's court here today for possessing contraband cigarettes at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Magistrate Suriani Ujang handed down the sentence to Zhang Yaojun, 48, and Zou Xinyi, 40, after they pleaded guilty to the charges, and ordered the sentences to run from their arrest on June 26.
The court also ordered the man and woman to pay import duties of RM9,200 each, or serve an additional one month in jail.
According to the charges, Zhang was alleged to have possessed 149 cartons of cigarettes, equivalent to 29,800 sticks, worth RM4,470, with assessed import duties amounting to RM20,770.60.
Zou was charged with possessing 311 cartons of cigarettes, equivalent to 62,200 sticks, worth RM9,330, with assessed import duties amounting to RM43,353.40.
Both were charged with committing the offence at the Passenger Examination Branch Office, KLIA Terminal 1 Customs Office, at 6pm on June 26.

The charge was framed under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967, punishable under Section 135(1)(v)(aa) of the same Act, which carries a minimum fine of 10 times the value of the goods or RM100,000, whichever is higher, and a maximum of 20 times the value or RM500,000, or a jail term of between six months and five years, or both, upon conviction.
KLIA Customs Department prosecuting officer Shahrul Amin Shahrul Nizam prosecuted, while lawyer Soon Sen Yang represented both accused.
Soon appealed for a lenient sentence, citing their family responsibilities and financial burdens.

"Zou is a single mother who is divorced and solely responsible for supporting her 10-year-old son, while Zhang has two schoolgoing children and his wife was involved in an accident several months ago," Soon said.

6ac37f1597b9fe3e: Take a selfie to see how healthy you are: the idea is enticing and this new research is promising. But so many factors have been ignored The idea that a single selfie could predict how long someone with cancer may live sounds like an incredible breakthrough. AI is getting better at spotting patterns in medical data, but can it be used to reliably predict what will happen to an individual patient? I asked a clinical colleague what she thought about the recent headlines. She found it an interesting development given that doctors have long used facial appearance to assess patient health. For example, she noted that they may write “appears stated age” or “appears older than stated age” as a proxy for general health. Now, researchers from Mass General Brigham, a healthcare institution in Massachusetts, have taken this idea a step further. They have developed an AI model trained on more than 40 million facial images – called FAHR-Face – to assess biological age and predict survival in cancer patients. For biological age, they developed FAHR-FaceAge, which estimates age from certain facial features such as the forehead, the wrinkles between the nose and mouth and the temples. For cancer survival, they developed FAHR-FaceSurvival, trained using almost 35,000 photos of cancer patients. This model focused more closely on the area below the eyes and the bridge of the nose – regions of the face “linked with dying”. Dr Raymond Mak, one of the study’s authors, noted that these parts of the face are the same as those referenced by Hippocrates in 400BC as signs of muscle wasting and mortality risk: “the nose sharp, the eyes sunken, the temples fallen in”. 49cb5c1b683dd187: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysians are still classified as “happy” as wages have recovered to above pre-Covid-19 levels, despite household spending rising rapidly among lower-income households, the Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) found in a recent survey.

The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, said median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, while labour force participation rose to 70.6 per cent that year.
Putrajaya recorded the fastest wage growth, with median monthly household income rising from RM2,700 in 2010 to more than RM4,500 in 2024.
However, the report also noted that nearly half of Malaysian households (46.2 per cent) lived in 22 of the country’s 166 districts, where median monthly household income was below RM7,017.
Some 111 of Malaysia’s 166 districts also recorded poverty rates above the national rate of 5.1 per cent. The poverty rate in 66 districts was more than twice the national rate, the report said.
Even as wages rise, lower-income households are spending more due to rising living costs, leaving them with little disposable income.
The report said household expenditure rose by more than 15 per cent among the bottom 70 per cent of the income distribution between 2019 and 2024.
However, spending barely changed among the top 10 per cent of households.
The squeeze was more severe for the bottom 10 per cent.

“Households in the bottom 10 per cent of the income distribution retained only 1.9 per cent of their gross incomes after covering their consumption expenses, down from 10.8 per cent in 2019,” KRI said in the report.
However, it noted that residual income does not account for tax payments, loan repayments or remittances to other households.
3092e3fc723e2ec0: SEOUL, Oct 23 — South Korea proposed today military talks with North Korea to “mutually confirm the precise location” of their border and discuss restoring communication channels, after an explosion in the DMZ further strained relations.

Tensions between the two Koreas have soared since the South last month blamed the blast inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) separating the countries on landmines laid by the North, an accusation it has fiercely rejected.

The South Korean defence ministry “formally proposes holding military talks with North Korea to mutually confirm the precise location of the land Military Demarcation Line (MDL) and discuss ways to restore military communication lines and prevent accidental clashes in border areas,” Kim Hong-cheol, deputy defense minister for policy, told reporters Friday.
The proposal comes just days after Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, announced that Pyongyang had moved new troop units into “firing position” along the border.
Seoul’s defence ministry said todayit was difficult to predict “what further incidents could occur if this situation is allowed to continue unaddressed”.
The ministry said that “three-way talks involving the United Nations Command would also be possible”.
“Specific dates and locations could be discussed through Panmunjom,” said Kim, referencing the symbolic truce village where troops from both Koreas stand face-to-face.
He added they hoped for “a positive response from North Korea”.
The South Korean defence ministry also noted that talks proposed last year with the North did not get a response from Pyongyang.

Seoul’s military on Tuesday accused Pyongyang of attempting to shift the blame for escalating military tensions, while confirming the use of loudspeakers and warning shots as “legitimate defensive measures to prevent North Korean troops from crossing the MDL and to drive back troops that have crossed it”.
Jin Yong-sung, chairman of South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff, also ordered the military to “respond with firm resolve” should North Korea use Seoul’s actions as a pretext for aggressive action.
Pyongyang has rejected claims it was behind the explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers inside the DMZ and mockingly dismissed calls for an apology.
The country on Monday called the situation along the border “grave”, saying it was considering deploying additional “tactical strike means” to the area.

Yesterday Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said the North would place loudspeakers on standby along the border “within days” and had put unspecified “new counter means” on alert.

South Korea’s foreign ministry also said Thursday it planned to send a letter to the president of the UN Security Council later in the day over the landmine incident, which it called a “clear violation of the armistice agreement”.
President Lee Jae Myung has called for the North to return to dialogue, an overture Kim Yo Jong later slammed as “the climax of the farce”. — AFP
8763f51982e5fa9e: KOTA BARU: The family of Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, who was allegedly murdered by her husband in Nilai, Negri Sembilan, hopes justice will be served.
Her brother, Mohd Hazwan Ibrahim, 38, said the family wanted the case to be thoroughly investigated and the suspect to face appropriate punishment.
"The family hopes that my late sister will get justice and that the suspect will receive a punishment befitting the crime," he said when contacted.
The suspect, who is in his 30s, has been remanded for another seven days, from Oct 23 to 29, to facilitate investigations into Norhazwani's death.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the extension would allow police to complete their investigations. The suspect was previously remanded for seven days from Oct 16.
Norhazwani, 35, was found dead at a government residential quarters in Nilai on Oct 15. Her husband later surrendered to police.
A post-mortem found that she died from pressure on her neck. Three stab wounds were also found on her body.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The couple had been married for seven years and had two daughters, aged five and six, who are now being cared for by their aunt in Tumpat.
477713d162ff0a2f: PUTRAJAYA: The Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) has recommended that the Department of Environment (DoE) step up nighttime inspections on scheduled waste (e-waste) and recycling premises to detect illegal activities more effectively.

The recommendation follows an EAIC investigation into DoE's enforcement on e-waste premises at the Segamat Industrial Area in Johor, which revealed that night inspections are currently conducted only on a need-to basis or upon receiving complaints.

In a statement today, the EAIC said its investigation, finalised during Commission Meeting No. 10/2026 on Oct 13, found that the DoE had conducted continuous enforcement, including taking appropriate action against repeat offenders.

The EAIC noted that the DoE carried out periodic inspections and took stern action against premises found violating the Environmental Quality Act 1974, as well as regulations regarding scheduled waste and licensing.
"Besides issuing field instructions, instruction notices, and compounds against offending premises, prosecution action was also taken against premises committing offences under Act 127," it said.

The EAIC conducted its probe through the Segamat 2.0 E-Waste Task Force to review the implementation of previously submitted improvement recommendations to the DoE, as well as investigate new enforcement allegations involving partial licenses, night operations, and repeat offences.

In a related development, the EAIC noted DoE's steps to enhance enforcement implementation, including reviewing standard operating procedures (SOPs), finalising compound guidelines, and updating procedures following amendments to the Environmental Quality Act 1974 that took effect on March 26, 2025.

The EAIC also noted that the DoE had upgraded its complaint management system by improving the myJAS Aduan application, accessible to the public at any time, alongside conducting regular training for its officers throughout 2025 and 2026.

Furthermore, the EAIC acknowledged the strengthening of delegation of enforcement powers through the Environmental Quality (Delegation of Powers to Government Departments, Local Authorities, and Corporations) Order 2025, which came into effect on July 8 last year.

Relevant enforcement agencies have also executed integrated actions through the Special Task Force on the Direction of Enforcement Management of Plastic Waste and E-Waste Importation into the Country, officially established on Dec 8, 2025.
The EAIC expressed hope that all related agencies will continue to intensify enforcement efforts to address e-waste issues comprehensively to safeguard environmental conservation.
c7e003196d9d85cf: KUALA LUMPUR: A Datuk Seri pleaded not guilty to criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM5.5 million and a separate money laundering offence involving RM403,000 at two Sessions Court today.
Former ARB Development Sdn Bhd director Datuk Seri Liew Kok Leong,53, entered his pleas after the charges were read out before judges Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad and Suzana Hussin.

Before Ilmami, Liew was accused of dishonestly misappropriating the company's RM5.5 million funds entrusted to him for the purchase of a 51 percent equity stake, comprising 255,000 ordinary shares, in C&M Renewable Energy Technology Sdn Bhd.

He allegedly transferred the money to the account of Messrs Ivan & Co for onward transfer to an account belonging to Er Yan Shuen, 55, purportedly for the purchase of three shop-office lots in Tigerlane Square in Ipoh, Perak.
The alleged offence occurred between May 6 and June 17, 2019 at Kuala Lumpur Sentral.
The charge framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code carries a maximum two-year jail term and not exceeding 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Julianazriana Jaafar sought bail of RM500,000 with one surety, in view of the substantial amount involved in the alleged offence and to ensure Liew's attendance in court.

She also applied for Liew to surrender his passport until case disposal, barred from leaving the country without court's permission, report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters monthly and refrain from harassing prosecution witnesses.
However, defence lawyer Zander Lim Wai Keong, asked for a reduced bail of RM50,000, arguing that the proposed sum was excessive and beyond his client's financial means.
"The bank accounts of my client as well as his family members had been frozen since August last year and affected their financial circumstances.
"My client cooperated with the MACC last year and never tried to evade investigations.
"He has no objections to his passport being impounded until case disposal and so, the issue of my client absconding is immaterial," he said, adding that Liew's wife would act as his surety.
After hearing the submissions, Ilmami set bail at RM200,000 with one surety.
He also ordered Liew to surrender his passport, report to the Putrajaya MACC headquarters monthly and not harass prosecution witnesses.
In the second case before Suzana, Liew pleaded not guilty to a money laundering charge involving RM403,000.

He was accused of being directly involved in a transaction involving proceeds from unlawful activities by instructing Er to transfer RM403,000 from his bank account to an account belonging to Permata Global Sdn Bhd through a cheque.
The alleged offence took place at a bank in Taman Maluri on June 15, 2019.
The charge brought under Section 4(1)(a) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 is punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.
Upon conviction, one faces a jail term not exceeding 15 years and a fine not less than five times the value of the illegal proceeds or RM5 million, whichever is higher.
Suzana allowed the bail terms imposed by Ilmami in the CBT case to apply to the money laundering case.
She also allowed the prosecution's application to transfer the case to Ilmami's court to be tried together.
The court fixed Dec 10 document submission.
After the proceedings, Lim said arrangements were being made for the payment of bail.

9e48ca647ee00b6b: STOCKHOLM: Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars said Friday it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide, as US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.
The company, owned by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor (US$6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23% from the same period last year.
It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.
"We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change," chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, "through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees".
The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.
In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

"We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges. However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient," Samuelsson said.
Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.
The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him "no later" than October next year.
c4bac075a4679347: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian lawyer Joanne Vengadesan has made history after being elected chair of Multilaw, a global network of law firms spanning over 100 countries.
The United Kingdom-based practitioner, who has 25 years of legal experience, was elected at Multilaw's Global Conference in Prague earlier this month.
She will serve a two-year term starting in September 2027, succeeding Australian lawyer Paul Kirton.
She began her career when she was called to the Malaysian Bar as an advocate and solicitor in 1997, initially practising intellectual property law in Kuala Lumpur.

Currently a partner at leading international firm Penningtons Manches Cooper LLP, Joanne is the daughter of retired Malaysian diplomat Datuk R. Vengadesan, who served as ambassador to several nations, including Italy and Namibia.
In a statement, Joanne said it was an honour to be named chair-elect and that she looks forward to assuming the role of chair next year.

"I love the perspective that being a Malaysian and working in the UK gives me. Malaysia is so multicultural that we grow up being so comfortable and at home with all our communities and cultures," she said.

Joanne said her international upbringing played a significant role in fostering her interest in being part of a global legal community, adding that her legal practice in the UK regularly handles cross-border matters.

"Multilaw has played a huge role in my career, and I am excited about the new challenges and opportunities to come. I could not be more proud of this network, which continues to go from strength to strength.

"The depth of the relationships and layers of connections between Multilaw member firms enable us to leverage the significant trust between us for the benefit of our respective clients. I am also very proud of my firm, Penningtons Manches Cooper's, continued commitment and active engagement across the network," she said.

Meanwhile, Penningtons Manches Cooper LLP chief executive officer Helen Drayton congratulated Joanne, describing her appointment as a testament to her talent, dedication, and close collaboration across the firm and the network.

Multilaw chief executive officer Adam Cooke, who has known Joanne for nearly 20 years, said he had witnessed first-hand her energy, insight, and warmth, adding that she understood the network's emphasis on strong relationships, mutual trust, and shared ambitions.

b0a78431a2d9a9dc: SINGAPORE: Actor Nick Teo is a true Good Samaritan who was brave enough to endure injections and donate his stem cells to save a life.
​The 37-year-old Singaporean actor and his wife, fellow actress Hong Ling, 32, are currently expecting their first child.
On Oct 21, Teo shared a video on Instagram documenting his donation journey.
Addressing common myths about the procedure, he wrote: "I know there are many rumours about bone marrow donation, including that it affects fertility."
"And here I am, about to start a family of my own. So I get why people might have concerns. "But do not let rumours stop you from finding out the facts."
In the post, Teo tagged The Bone Marrow Donor Programme—an organisation managing Singapore's only register of volunteer bone marrow donors.
Their aim is to bring hope to patients with leukaemia and blood-related illnesses, with a goal of finding a match for every patient.
​The clip shows Teo giving himself injections to increase the stem cell count in his blood prior to donation, with his wife helping him with the first jab.
​He admitted: "I was quite nervous at first. But after going through the whole process, I realised it was not as scary as I thought."
​"Even after giving himself another injection on a different day, he said he felt "quite okay".
​In his caption, Teo explained that the actual donation felt similar to giving blood, "taking about six hours of my life to give someone else a second chance at theirs".
​Addressing worries that donating makes a person weak, Teo shared that after a few days of rest, he was right back to doing what he loves. The video
Nick Teo has debunked bone marrow donation myths to save lives (INSTAGRAM/NICK TEO)
showed him filming a boxing scene for the Mediacorp crime drama In His Hands.
​"But look at me," he added. "I am still filming fight scenes."

​Teo ended his post by encouraging others to sign up as potential donors: "If you have ever thought about signing up, maybe this is your little nudge. A simple swab could lead to something life-changing. You never know whose life you might save."
"To me, donating stem cells was just a small part of my life.
"But to someone else, it could mean getting a second chance at life.
"And who knows? Maybe you could be someone's hope too," he added.

51463e6df621e1dd: HEBRON: Israeli troops on Friday shot dead two suspected Palestinian assailants in the West Bank after a shooting that left at least five people wounded, officials said.

2e02cca1a0ccbd66: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has not ruled out imposing a nationwide ban on the Waze navigation application once suitable alternatives become available, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the government was assessing alternative navigation applications following its decision to bar civil servants from using Waze over national security concerns.
"I will not allow civil servants to use it under any circumstances. Waze is banned.

"We need to study the available alternatives. If we find that their capabilities are sufficiently developed, we may consider using the facilities available," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Al-Mustaqim in Taman Nirwana, Ampang, today.
Anwar said the government had acted after examining Waze's links to Israel and the legal jurisdiction governing its terms of use.
He said he had instructed officials to verify the information during a cybersecurity meeting earlier this week.
"When I received the information, we checked it. First, its headquarters is based in Israel.
"Second, under the agreement, if you use Waze and a problem arises, Israeli law applies," he said.
Anwar defended the speed of the decision, saying the government could not afford to compromise on national security.
On Wednesday, the government announced a ban on Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's status as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
The government also encouraged the use of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu.
Waze has rejected allegations that it collects sensitive government information or allows third parties to exploit users' personal data.
A Waze spokesperson described the allegations as "completely untrue."
"Waze operates under strict privacy policies to protect user data and complies with global legal data protection standards," the spokesperson said.

The National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) has acknowledged that there is no evidence Waze has analysed users' movement patterns in the manner feared by the government, but maintained that the potential for such analysis remains a security risk.
The agency said location information, travel routes and other data collected over time could reveal users' movements and daily routines.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo also clarified in Parliament yesterday that the existing ban applies only to civil servants performing official duties and does not extend to the general public.
He said Malaysians remained free to use other navigation applications, including Google Maps.
Waze, which was developed in Israel, was acquired by Google in 2013.

032f7be537582658: PHILLIP ISLAND (Australia): Marco Bezzecchi recovered from a crash to top the timesheets ahead of Raul Fernandez in Australian MotoGP practice Friday interrupted by a wallaby hopping onto the track.
The Italian Aprilia rider clocked a blistering lap of 1min 26.775sec at the death around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit – which is hosting its final MotoGP – in warm but windy conditions.
Rain is forecast for the weekend.
Ducati world champion Marc Marquez was third and Ai Ogura on his Aprilia fourth.
Championship leader Jorge Martin, who is two points clear of Marquez with five rounds of the season left, was fifth fastest.
Bezzecchi, who won last week in Indonesia and is third in the standings, finished 0.072 ahead of last year's Australian grand prix winner Fernandez, with Marquez 0.054 further adrift.
The top 10 are exempt from Q1 qualifying on Saturday and guaranteed a top 12 grid placing in both the afternoon sprint race and Sunday's MotoGP.
Among those missing out on the top 10 were Francesco Bagnaia and Fabio Quartararo.
Bezzecchi fell at Turn 4 early in the session after clipping the back of Alex Marquez which sent him sliding off with his bike landing on his right leg.
A second red flag came out soon after the resumption when a wallaby was spotted on the track.
Martin was leading at the time and when they got underway again the Spaniard was surpassed by a recovered Bezzecchi and then Marc Marquez.
Marquez was the first to go under 1:27 with eight minutes left before Bezzecchi and Fernandez stormed past him as the clock ticked down.
There was plenty of carnage in morning practice which was topped by Marc Marquez with Fernandez, Iker Lecuona, and Jack Miller all suffering nasty falls while Brad Binder had a big engine failure.
Pramac Yamaha pair Miller and Augusto Fernandez, and Alex Marquez, came off in the afternoon run.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide. - AFP

77efdaf4397da3c5: IPOH: Independent preacher Ustaz Wadi Annuar was discharged from hospital after being involved in a three-vehicle accident along the East-West Highway near Gerik early today.

He said eight people were involved in the accident, which also involved a Perodua Myvi and a Perodua Bezza.
"Four people were injured, while four others escaped unhurt. No fatalities were reported," he said in a statement.

The car entered the opposite lane and sideswiped the oncoming Bezza before crashing into the Vellfire, which was travelling behind it.

All injured victims were taken to Gerik Hospital for treatment, with two later referred to Taiping Hospital.

Police advised motorists to exercise caution when driving on winding roads during rainy conditions, reduce speed, and ensure their vehicles remain under control.
26f9b307d8b6ebd8: TOKYO, Oct 23 — The head of the Asian Football Confederation today said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as Fifa president following fierce criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan.
The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the AFC when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing.

The AFC in August had joined Uefa (Europe) and Concacaf (North and Central America and the Caribbean) in condemning Infantino over his plan to open Fifa’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino has faced calls to quit and has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.

“I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as Fifa president,” said Sheikh Salman, in a significant boost to Infantino’s prospects.
“I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent.
“I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.”
Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past.
“But let’s not relate the two things together. We need to move forward... football is strongest when we work together.”
Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed project, has headed Fifa since 2016 and is running for re-election in March.
The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.
No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him so far, despite outspoken condemnation especially from Europe.
Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his relationship with US President Donald Trump. — AFP
fe75603b40c1ef00: SEOUL; SK Hynix on Friday put on hold a planned US listing for its Solidigm chip unit due to market volatility — a move which also comes after South Korean authorities raised concerns that the deal could undermine shareholder interests.

A listing of Solidigm, a former Intel business that specialises in NAND flash memory and solid-state drives, had been under consideration to help fund a new US factory and meet surging demand for chips in AI data centres.
It could also have funded share cancellations and buybacks, SK Hynix said in a statement.
People familiar with the now-suspended IPO plans had said that the share sale could have raised US$15 billion and valued the unit at US$150 billion.

The South Korean chip giant, which became dual-listed with a debut on the Nasdaq in July, said it plans to continue to explore ways to fund Solidigm's expansion and enhance shareholder value, including reviewing the timing, scale and financing of future investments.
"This decision does not reflect any change in Solidigm's growth prospects or investment needs," it said.

It was not immediately clear how the decision would be received by the Trump administration, which has put pressure on foreign chipmakers to build new facilities in the US and which has been holding discussions with SK Hynix.

According to people familiar with the matter, SK Hynix has sought to use the prospect of a potential factory in the US as a bargaining chip, linking it to hoped-for approval from Washington that would allow US chipmaking equipment to be exported to China to increase production there.

South Korean authorities have said they are discussing semiconductor investments in the US with Washington as part of broader bilateral talks, but they are not part of negotiations about a US$350-billion investment commitment South Korea made to the US last year in exchange for lower US tariffs.

Across the globe, sentiment towards AI and chip-related stocks has retreated sharply as investors increasingly fret over whether rising interest rates will mean that companies involved in building out the AI supply chain will make sufficient earnings to repay their debts.
At the same time, in South Korea, concerns have also mounted that a listing of Solidigm in the US would dilute the interests of SK Hynix shareholders.

Financial Supervisory Service governor Lee Chan-jin told a parliamentary hearing this week that regulators were examining whether Solidigm's potential US IPO would require a review under the country's dual-listing restrictions, which were tightened in July to strengthen shareholder protections.

In addition to broad concerns about the AI sector, worries that a Solidigm IPO could dilute SK Hynix shareholders' interests have weighed on the chipmaker's shares, which have tumbled 31% since news of the potential listing emerged in late September.
That compares with a 20% decline in the benchmark KOSPI index over the same period.
The Korea Corporate Governance Forum, an independent body, welcomed SK Hynix's decision.

Instead of a US listing for Solidigm, the chipmaker, which has made massive earnings gains on the AI boom, could instead inject capital through its AI Company entity, even if Solidigm requires tens of trillions of won in capital expenditure, it said.
Citing average estimates from South Korean brokerages, it said SK Hynix’s cash holdings were projected to reach ₩456 trillion (US$344 billion) by the end of 2027.
SK Hynix shares were up 1.4% in afternoon trade, outperforming a 1.4% decline in the KOSPI.
e8693a33ac2a03c9: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has appealed against a High Court ruling allowing Perikatan Nasional to resume its political activities, including contesting next month's Melaka election.

The notice of appeal, dated today, was filed by the Attorney-General's Chambers on behalf of Registrar of Societies (RoS) director-general Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md granted PN's application to stay the RoS suspension and deregistration orders pending the disposal of its judicial review.
According to the notice sighted by the New Straits Times, the two appellants were dissatisfied with the High Court's decision allowing the stay application sought by PN.
Azizan allowed PN's application to stay the RoS decision revoking the opposition coalition's registration, as well as an earlier notice suspending all its political activities.
The ruling effectively cleared the way for PN to continue its political activities, including campaigning and contesting the Melaka state election scheduled for Nov 14.
The judge said exceptional circumstances warranted the stay, particularly considering the potential impact on the political rights of party members and elected representatives.
He said the court also took into account the possible irreversible consequences of preventing PN from participating in elections.
The judge ruled that granting the stay would not prejudice the authorities, as PN's political activities could still be monitored and enforcement action taken if any laws were breached.
On Oct 20, the RoS announced that PN's registration had been revoked after finding that the coalition's explanation in response to a show-cause notice was unsatisfactory.
The deregistration followed an earlier order issued under Section 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966, suspending all PN activities effective Sept 23.
6596ea3be8dbd048: KUANTAN: Local authorities in Pahang are finalising transport links to East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) stations in Kuantan, Temerloh, Maran, and Bentong ahead of its Dec 12 launch.

Pahang Public Works, Transport, and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim said the initiative aims to improve public transport links between ECRL stations and surrounding areas, making it easier for commuters to reach their destinations.
The ECRL, which will connect Kota Baru to the Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal via Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor, is scheduled to begin operations on Dec 12.

"Improved access routes will ensure smoother integration between rail services and local transport networks, including bus terminals, allowing passengers to travel to and from ECRL stations with ease.

"Shuttle and stage buses are among the measures being considered, alongside taxis and e-hailing services. We do not want commuters to be stranded or left waiting for hours at stations due to inadequate transport links.
"These improvements will ease travel, particularly for residents living far from the stations, and encourage more people to use the rail service," he told the New Straits Times today.
On Oct 19, the ECRL announced that economy-class fares between Gombak and Kota Baru would start at RM125. The service is targeting 1.4 million passengers annually from next year.
Pahang has seven ECRL stations, located in Temerloh, Bentong, Maran, Paya Besar, Kota SAS, Kuantan Port City and Cherating.

Meanwhile, Razali said plans were underway to develop an integrated public transport terminal at Paya Besar ECRL Station in Gambang here, as well as an integrated terminal with a commercial centre at Bentong ECRL Station.

He said the four local authorities - Kuantan City Council, Temerloh Municipal Council, Bentong Municipal Council and Maran District Council - were also responsible for formulating Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) plans within their respective jurisdictions.

The TOD plans include Pahangku Apartments, administrative and commercial centres, hotels, business complexes, mixed-use developments, community institutions and facilities within a 15km radius of each ECRL station.
b860769d143b2077: PHILIP ISLAND: Marco Bezzecchi recovered from a crash to top the timesheets ahead of Raul Fernandez in Australian MotoGP practice Friday interrupted by a wallaby hopping onto the track.
The Italian Aprilia rider clocked a blistering lap of 1min 26.775sec at the death around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit - which is hosting its final MotoGP - in warm but windy conditions.
Rain is forecast for the weekend.
Ducati world champion Marc Marquez was third and Ai Ogura on his Aprilia fourth.
Championship leader Jorge Martin, who is two points clear of Marquez with five rounds of the season left, was fifth fastest.
Bezzecchi, who won last week in Indonesia and is third in the standings, finished 0.072 ahead of last year's Australian grand prix winner Fernandez, with Marquez 0.054 further adrift.
The top 10 are exempt from Q1 qualifying on Saturday and guaranteed a top 12 grid placing in both the afternoon sprint race and Sunday's MotoGP.
Among those missing out on the top 10 were Francesco Bagnaia and Fabio Quartararo.
Bezzecchi fell at Turn 4 early in the session after clipping the back of Alex Marquez which sent him sliding off with his bike landing on his right leg.
A second red flag came out soon after the resumption when a wallaby was spotted on the track.
Martin was leading at the time and when they got underway again the Spaniard was surpassed by a recovered Bezzecchi and then Marc Marquez.
Marquez was the first to go under 1:27 with eight minutes left before Bezzecchi and Fernandez stormed past him as the clock ticked down.
There was plenty of carnage in morning practice which was topped by Marc Marquez with Fernandez, Iker Lecuona, and Jack Miller all suffering nasty falls while Brad Binder had a big engine failure.
Pramac Yamaha pair Miller and Augusto Fernandez, and Alex Marquez, came off in the afternoon run.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide.
