208ea77694333d2f: IPOH, Oct 23 — The issue of stray animals in the country has sparked growing public concern, particularly in recent times, with a series of incidents involving public safety, including the threat of disease, being reported.
Stakeholders say resorting to the capture and culling of stray animals is not a sustainable solution, calling instead for a more humane, long-term approach involving all relevant parties.
They said this should include raising awareness among pet owners and the public, with animal welfare at its core.
Animal welfare is also recognised as one of the approaches under the Ihsan (compassion) principle of the Malaysia Madani concept.
Subsidised sterilisation under Perak Pawsitive

The main reason for the growing stray animal population is not simply their natural reproductive instinct, but also the irresponsible behaviour of owners who fail to sterilise their cats and dogs and allow them to roam freely on the streets.
Some owners also abandon their pets for various reasons, including being unable to afford their upkeep as the number of animals in their care increases.

Studies and data from leading international animal welfare organisations, including the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals and the International Animal Protection and Welfare Alliance indicate that an unsterilised female cat or dog can produce between 12 and 18 offspring a year.
Without sterilisation, their descendants could contribute to a population of up to 12,000 animals within five years.

Consequently, international bodies, including the World Organisation for Animal Health, recognise sterilisation as one of the most effective measures to address the growing population of pets and stray animals.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Perak Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching shows a Perak Pawsitive Initiative leaflet at the Perak Darul Ridzuan Building in Ipoh recently. — Bernama pic

In response to calls from stakeholders, the Perak state government has taken proactive steps through a preventive sterilisation programme implemented in strategic collaboration with non-governmental organisations under the Perak Pawsitive Initiative, also known as Perak Pawsitive.

State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said 14 programme sessions had been conducted since the initiative was introduced in 2024, resulting in the sterilisation of 2,402 dogs and cats to date.
“The programme involves cross-sector collaboration with government agencies and NGOs comprising animal lovers, and has now attracted participation from the private sector.
“It began with an allocation of RM150,000, which was subsequently doubled to RM300,000 this year following encouraging public response and the urgent needs on the ground,” she told Bernama.

She said the funds were used to implement subsidised sterilisation campaigns, prioritising dogs and selected cats, as well as educational programmes and the publication of a responsible pet ownership booklet, which must be distributed when owners apply for or renew their animal licences.
Under the subsidised programme, the Perak government provides a subsidy of RM80 for sterilising male and female dogs and RM40 for cats of either sex.
The regular fees are RM180 for dogs and RM120 for cats.
Currently, four veterinary clinics are collaborating with Perak Pawsitive, with each two-day programme session targeting 50 dogs and 70 cats for sterilisation.

Sandrea said the initiative also promotes pet adoption through the message ‘Adopt for Life, Never Abandon’, while seeking to raise public awareness of responsible pet ownership and address the root causes of stray animal problems.
Microchipping to identify pet owners
Apart from sterilisation, another measure being planned under the initiative is an identification system using microchips.

Sandrea said the microchips, which store information about owners and the animals’ vaccination and sterilisation status, would be implanted in pet dogs and linked to the licensing systems of local authorities.
“Microchipping is important in our efforts to address irresponsible ownership practices, including the failure to sterilise animals.
“We want to reduce unplanned breeding so that pets do not produce unwanted generations.
“If owners abandon their dogs, we can trace them through the microchips and take action against those responsible.
“We see microchipping as another measure that complements what we are already doing,” she said, adding that the chips would be implanted when owners applied for dog licences from local authorities.
However, she said the proposal was still at the feasibility study stage.

The state government was also considering harmonising dog licensing requirements across all 15 local authorities, while assessing the availability of veterinary services and the cost implications for the public.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Ipoh Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals chairman Ricky Soong (right) feeds a dog at the ISPCA shelter. — Bernama pic

Sandrea said a pilot project to map people who feed stray animals, known as feeder mapping, was also being implemented through the Ipoh City Council to establish a more accurate picture of the feeding community and the stray animal population in Perak.
“The state government is implementing this initiative through https://pawsitive.my/.
“To make the mapping exercise successful, we need to identify and register the feeders.
“This will also help empower the feeder community.
“We understand that those feeding stray animals are animal lovers who do so out of compassion.
“However, this can sometimes lead to problems involving cleanliness and complaints from the public.

“By bringing them together, registering them and providing training and briefings, we hope to ensure they become responsible feeders who help address the problem rather than create issues related to cleanliness,” she said.
She expressed hope that the registered feeder community would assist the state government in gathering data on stray animals on the ground.
She added that the state government was also considering offering suitable sites to relevant NGOs to establish animal shelters at nominal rental rates.
NGO concerns and proposals for #ProjekTogetherBoleh and #ExecuteTNVRM

While the subsidised sterilisation programme is seen as a positive first step, animal welfare advocates say it must be expanded to cover stray animals through cooperation with NGOs and independent stray animal activists.
Ipoh Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (ISPCA) chairman Ricky Soong said the campaign should be intensified to curb the growing population of animals at risk of becoming strays.
“Without sterilisation, animal populations can multiply rapidly within just a few years.
“As a result, these animals eventually end up abandoned in residential areas, construction sites and factories,” he said.

He said ISPCA alone cared for more than 300 dogs, incurring thousands of ringgit in monthly expenses, excluding medical treatment, vaccination, health screening and redemption fees when animals are caught by local authorities.
He said the need to pay redemption fees for impounded animals had placed the organisation under severe financial strain, as its operations depended on public donations.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
(From left) Furkids Haven chairman Irene Boey, ISPCA chairman Ricky Soong and independent feeder Peggy Vong show the equipment used for procedures on stray animals in Ipoh. — Bernama pic

Furkids Haven chairman Irene Boey said that between July 2025 and July this year, cumulative figures compiled from several NGOs and independent feeders showed that RM103,900 had been spent on redemption fees paid to local authorities.
“Statistics show that from August 1 to the middle of this month, the number of dogs caught in Ipoh alone had reached 360.
“Of these, 12 had to be put to sleep because of the tight three-day deadline, as well as a lack of funds and shelter space to redeem them,” she said.

In view of the situation, ExecuteAWA national humanitarian movement founder Sue Ann Kong proposed #ProjekTogetherBoleh, described as Malaysia’s first national preventive framework specifically designed to manage stray animal populations in a comprehensive and strategic manner.
She said the framework focused on science-based data collection and preventive measures to address the stray animal issue.
“The culling of stray animals has been proven ineffective from a scientific perspective because of the vacuum effect.
“When local authorities capture and cull animals in a particular area, the area becomes temporarily vacant.
“However, because food sources and shelter remain available, new groups of stray animals move into the same area.
“This is a natural ecological phenomenon that causes the cycle of animal overpopulation to continue without resolution,” Sue Ann explained.
She said #ProjekTogetherBoleh proposed the implementation of #ExecuteTNVRM as a comprehensive solution.

The approach goes beyond conventional sterilisation and incorporates several critical components: ‘T’ for Trap, involving the humane capture of stray animals; ‘N’ for Neuter, to effectively control reproduction; ‘V’ for Vaccinate, including rabies vaccination and parasite control; ‘R’ for Rehome, Reclaim or Release; and ‘M’ for Microchipping and Manage.
Sue Ann said ExecuteAWA had developed a specialised statistical model using reverse engineering, taking into account realistic variables such as mortality, reproduction and population decline rates.
“Through this data modelling, the impact of implementing #ProjekTogetherBoleh can be measured clearly.

“For example, a study model for Langkawi estimated that the population of stray dogs, which stood at about 3,900 in 2024, could surge to 46,000 within 10 years without structured reproductive control.

“If #ProjekTogetherBoleh were implemented systematically, with a targeted sterilisation rate of 70 per cent, the population could potentially decline to just 235 within the same period, at an effectiveness rate of up to 94 per cent,” she said.

She said the #ProjekTogetherBoleh initiative had been implemented since November 2025 in collaboration with the Rembau District Council in Negeri Sembilan and continued through the PTB 3.0 series in Seremban.
ExecuteAWA stressed that successfully addressing the issue required firm commitment and cooperation from all stakeholders, including ministries, local authorities, local NGOs and the wider community.
“We hope to work with more state governments, including Perak.
“We need to move away from reactive measures towards preventive action,” she said.
Sterilisation must meet medical and animal welfare standards

From a scientific and medical perspective, sterilisation procedures, involving the removal of the testes in males or ovaries in females, are recognised as effective in preventing uncontrolled reproduction.

Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris Faculty of Technical and Vocational head of the Department of Agricultural Science Dr Fazhana Ismail said the procedure could also reduce animals’ tendency to roam in search of mates due to hormonal urges.
However, she stressed that sterilisation must comply with strict animal welfare guidelines.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Animals are sterilised under the Perak Pawsitive Initiative’s cat and dog sterilisation awareness campaign at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council rest house hall. — Bernama pic
Surgical procedures must be performed by registered veterinary practitioners, while the use of anaesthesia and pain relief is essential to prevent unnecessary suffering.
“Animals must also receive proper post-operative care until they have fully recovered.
“Nevertheless, sterilisation is not a magic solution that instantly makes every animal tame.
“Rather, it is a long-term biological intervention and one of the most ethical ways to stop unwanted breeding cycles,” she said.

She said the approach pioneered by the Perak state government through Perak Pawsitive, supported by the science-based framework advocated by NGOs such as ExecuteAWA, could pave the way for more humane population control efforts.
2c62b444701beba0: TAWAU: A 19-year-old who was previously ordered to perform community service for offering sexual services was jailed for six months by the magistrate's court here today after repeating the offence.
Nurul Syahfathin Puteri Sofea pleaded guilty after the charge under Section 372B of the Penal Code was read before magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum.
According to the charge, she offered sexual services via WhatsApp in a rented room at Flat Sabindo, Jalan Habib Sheikh, Bandar Sabindo, at 9.30pm on Oct 20.
Based on the facts of the case, an undercover police officer contacted her via WhatsApp, after which she offered sexual services for RM150.
Police raided the room and seized two condoms, RM150 in cash and a key.
During proceedings, the magistrate asked the unrepresented accused how long she had been involved in such activities.
She replied that this was her first time on this occasion.
When asked why she had engaged in the activity at a young age, she said she was desperate to pay overdue rent after losing her job and claimed her wages had not been paid.
She said she had previously worked as an assistant at a food stall.
However, prosecuting officer Assistant Superintendent Nur Intan Jamrin told the court that the accused had committed the same offence and was charged at the same court on Sept 4 last year.
The court was told that she had been ordered to perform community service for six months, four hours a day, and placed under a RM1,000 bond without deposit.
Don Stiwin reprimanded the accused for repeating the offence despite being given a second chance.
"I gave you a chance for six months previously, but you still repeated the same offence. At your young age, you were given an opportunity but you still did it," he said.
The court sentenced her to six months' jail from the date of her arrest.
f84bb3369fdecb78: LONDON: General Motors (GM), the biggest customer of a US factory making rare earth magnets for electric vehicles (EVs), cancelled its long-term supply deal with the manufacturer, and the two sides are in arbitration, according to regulatory documents and a person with knowledge of the situation.
The move spotlights the challenges Western firms face in building domestic rare-earths output and cutting their reliance on China, which produces about 90% of global permanent magnets.
It also shows how the US auto industry's landscape has changed since Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025 and cut federal support for EVs.
Germany's Vacuumschmelze, or VAC, signed a long-term deal in 2023 with GM to supply permanent magnets for its EVs from a new plant in South Carolina.

Energy Fuels, which agreed in June to pay US$1.9 billion to acquire VAC, said in US Securities and Exchange Commission documents filed last week that a customer of the plant terminated its supply agreement on July 1, and VAC launched arbitration proceedings against that customer several days later.

It did not name the customer, but GM this week reported in an SEC filing that a supplier of a component for EV traction motors "initiated an arbitration against us seeking damages after we terminated a strategic sourcing agreement," without saying why it cancelled the deal.
The person familiar with the matter confirmed GM was the customer that cancelled the contract with VAC's US unit, e-VAC Magnetics.
GM and Energy Fuels declined to comment on the arbitration because it is confidential.
The dispute has not been previously reported and none of the companies involved have issued press releases about the issue.

VAC launched its US$500-million US magnet plant late last year with a capacity of just under 2,000 metric tonnes a year, and 90% was set to be sold to GM, with the remainder supplying the US government, VAC CEO Erik Eschen told Reuters in September last year.
VAC's US unit said it was seeking damages in arbitration due to wrongful termination.
"We have no concerns about VAC’s commercial success and its ability to produce rare earth permanent magnets to customer specifications," Energy Fuels said.
However, Energy Fuels told Reuters there may be "potential adjustments to our purchase price of VAC depending on the outcome of the arbitration".
GM rolls back EV sales
GM has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration’s withdrawal of incentives and tax breaks meant to benefit the industry.
In January, GM took a US$6 billion charge to unwind some EV investments.
When GM and VAC announced the supply deal three years ago, VAC said the plant would support GM for a minimum of 10 years and supply a wide range of models.
The dispute first arose in April 2026, according to the SEC documents. Energy Fuels said it was aware of the dispute when it was negotiating the VAC acquisition.

Energy Fuels, a producer of uranium for the nuclear power industry, said the takeover would allow it to become one of the world's largest non-Chinese producers of magnets used in the aerospace, defence and renewable energy sectors.
VAC supplies magnets to more than 1,000 customers, from facilities in Germany, Malaysia and other countries.

53e240884365ad2b: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has appointed former Bursa Malaysia Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Umar Swift as its new group managing director and chief executive officer, effective Jan 1, 2027.
Hong Leong Capital Bhd, HLIB's parent company, said Umar will succeed Lee Jim Leng, who is retiring after more than 17 years at the helm of the investment bank.
Lee has served as HLIB's group managing director and chief executive officer since 2009, overseeing its growth across capital markets, brokerage and advisory services.
Hong Leong Capital chairman Tan Kong Khoon thanked Lee for her leadership and contributions to HLIB and Malaysia's investment banking industry.
"Under her stewardship, HLIB has achieved significant milestones and built a resilient foundation for the future. We wish her a very well-deserved, happy, and fulfilling retirement," he said.
Umar brings extensive experience across banking, insurance and capital markets.
He previously served as Bursa Malaysia's chief executive officer and MAA Group Bhd's chief executive officer and group managing director.
He also held the position of head of Enterprise Financial Services Group at Malayan Banking Bhd.
Tan said Umar's experience in leading financial institutions and his understanding of Malaysia's capital markets would support HLIB's next phase of growth.

"We are pleased to welcome Umar to HLIB. His understanding of Malaysia's capital markets and experience in leading financial institutions will be valuable as we build on the strong foundation Jim Leng and the team have established.
"We look forward to working with him and our colleagues at HLIB to deepen client relationships, grow the business and support our clients' evolving financing and investment needs," he said.

4c14e083234fa3d0: KUALA LUMPUR: Former ARB Development Sdn Bhd director Liew Kok Leong was charged today with criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM5.5 million and money laundering involving RM403,000.
Liew, 53, pleaded not guilty to both charges, which were read before separate sessions court judges – Ilmami Ahmad and Suzana Hussin.

Before Ilmami, Liew claimed trial to a CBT charge involving the alleged misappropriation of RM5.5 million belonging to ARB Development, which was intended to finance the purchase of a 51% equity stake, comprising 255,000 ordinary shares, in C&M Renewable Energy Technology Sdn Bhd.
He is accused of transferring the funds to Messrs Ivan & Co for onward transfer to a bank account belonging to Er Yan Shuen, purportedly for the purchase of three office lots in Ipoh, Perak.
The offence allegedly took place between May and June 2019.
The charge was framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

Ilmami set bail at RM200,000 and ordered Liew to surrender his passport to the court pending the disposal of the case. Liew was also required to report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission office once a month.

Before Suzana, Liew was charged with money laundering involving RM403,000, by allegedly directing Er to transfer the proceeds of unlawful activity from his Maybank account to Permata Global Sdn Bhd's CIMB Bank account on June 15, 2019.
The charge was framed under Section 4(1)(a) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
The section provides for imprisonment of up to 15 years and a fine of at least five times the value of the proceeds of unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
Suzana adopted the bail amount set by Ilmami.
Lawyer Zander Lim represented Liew while deputy public prosecutor Julianazriana Jaafar appeared for the prosecution.
4b34525859f3e7a1: PETALING JAYA: An architect has claimed trial at the Ampang magistrates’ court to a charge of molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Melawati.
Saiful Anuar Abdul Aziz, 61, pleaded not guilty when the charge was read to him before magistrate Siti Nurul Ain Arifin.
He is accused of using criminal force against the 18-year-old victim by touching several parts of his body with the intention of outraging his modesty, Berita Harian reported.
The offence was allegedly committed at 7.10pm on Oct 18 in a sauna room at a gymnasium in a shopping mall.
The charge was framed under Section 354 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, whipping or any two of these punishments upon conviction.

Siti Nurul allowed the accused bail of RM9,000 with one surety. She also ordered him not to tamper with the prosecution witnesses and to surrender his passport to the court pending the conclusion of the case.
Deputy public prosecutor M Ramanathan Alias Ashwin handled the prosecution while the accused was represented by counsel K Theivaendran.
The court fixed Nov 26 for mention.
161441b9fc5b1576: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) will conduct the next iteration of the National Risk Assessment in 2027, enabling a deeper assessment of the money laundering and terrorism financing risks facing the Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBP) sectors.
Deputy Governor Datuk Marzunisham Omar said the findings will support the development of more targeted policies, guidance, and mitigation measures tailored to the specific risks faced by each sector.

“Your practical insights will be essential. They will help ensure that our policy responses remain effective, proportionate and grounded in the realities faced by each sector,” he said in his welcoming remarks at DNFBP Compliance Conference 2026, held yesterday.

According to BNM, DNFBP refers to a group that consists of a parent company incorporated in Malaysia or any other type of legal person exercising control and coordinating functions over the rest of the group, together with branches and/or subsidiaries that are subject to anti-money laundering (AML), countering the financing of terrorism (CFT) and countering proliferation financing (CPF) policies and procedures at the group level.
Meanwhile, Marzunisham said the AML, CFT and CPF framework depends not only on strong laws and sound policies, but also on credible supervision and enforcement.
He said the central bank takes non-compliance seriously, as weaknesses in any part of the system could undermine the integrity of Malaysia’s entire AML/CFT framework.
Recent joint enforcement actions involving regulatory and law enforcement agencies reinforce this point.

BNM and the Companies Commission of Malaysia (CCM) recently took enforcement action against a company secretary for failing to submit suspicious transaction reports relating to foreign nationals suspected to be involved in an international scam syndicate.

A Labuan investment bank was subjected to enforcement action by BNM and the Labuan Financial Services Authority (LFSA) following material deficiencies in customer due diligence. This affected the firm’s ability to assess customers’ potential involvement in illicit overseas activities, as well as delays in submitting suspicious transaction reports.
“These cases may involve different sectors and circumstances, but they convey the same message: Weak due diligence, vigilance and reporting create space for criminals to operate.
“Professional services must never become the gate through which illicit funds acquire the appearance of legitimacy, whether knowingly or unknowingly,” Marzunisham added. — Bernama
555cbd6ffd8ed21e: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Canadian jet maker Bombardier was investing US$270 million in the United States, days after he dropped threats to ban the company from the country.

Trump's September threats against Bombardier became a political issue in Kansas, where it employs 1,500 people in Wichita. The threatened ban prompted calls to the White House from Kansas lawmakers, including Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is facing a tough race in the Nov 3 elections.

In a Truth Social post late on Thursday, Trump said Bombardier's investment would create thousands of jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana, and credited Marshall along with Texas attorney general Ken Paxton for the deal.

"Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas has done an incredible job in representing his Great State! Because of him, working together with the Trump Administration, Bombardier is investing 270 MILLION DOLLARS, creating THOUSANDS of American Jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana," he said.
"Senator Marshall, together with Attorney General Ken Paxton of Texas, has done an incredible job in getting this Deal done."
Bombardier, which announced a US$50 million investment in Wichita last week, did not respond to a request for comment on the investment details announced by Trump.
At a speech in Wichita on Monday, Trump had said he did not plan to hurt Bombardier and would take care of its workers.
"... now I find out they have a presence here, and we're not hurting them if they're in Kansas. So we'll take care of those people and the jobs," the president said in that speech.

In February, Trump had threatened to decertify Bombardier aircraft over a certification dispute involving rival Gulfstream Aerospace. That threat never materialised because Transport Canada ultimately approved the jets.
fb7717e5a6736a27: KUALA LUMPUR: The Registrar of Societies (RoS) and home minister have filed an appeal against the High Court’s decision to stay Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) deregistration.
A notice of appeal sighted by FMT names RoS director-general Zulfikar Ahmad and home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as the appellants.
It states that both are dissatisfied with the ruling delivered by Justice Azizan Arshad yesterday.
The notice was filed by a senior federal counsel on behalf of the two appellants.
PN lawyer Rafique Rashid Ali confirmed the filing.
The stay granted by the High Court will remain in force pending the outcome of the coalition’s judicial review application.
Azizan ruled that exceptional circumstances warranted a stay, citing PN’s political role and the implications for its rights as elected representatives and state governments.

On Oct 5, PN filed a judicial review application against the RoS, seeking, among others, a certiorari order to quash the Sept 23 notice suspending the coalition’s activities indefinitely and a Sept 22 show-cause notice requiring it to explain why it should not be deregistered.
PN also sought a declaration that both notices were null and void.
The application was filed by the secretaries-general of five PN component parties, excluding Bersatu.
0237a586ba5f439f: BEIJING: China ordered an "all-out" rescue effort in Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured dozens and flattened hundreds of homes, state media reported.
Footage showed rescue workers with torches clambering in the dark through some of the more than 300 houses that Xinhua said collapsed in the 7.0-magnitude quake on Thursday evening.
Diners ran out of restaurants and items fell off wobbling supermarket shelves as the tremor struck, according to clips on state broadcaster CCTV, which said 65 people were injured.
One resident told local media that her family had just gone to bed when her home shook, knocking over objects, and that they "rushed outside without even taking the time to get dressed".
"My legs were shaking the entire time I was heading downstairs and by the time I reached the bottom, I was so terrified that I burst into tears," the woman said.
Local residents "are afraid to return to their homes," she said. "They set up tents along the roadside or spent the night in their cars," she added.
A man told the Beijing News that the "very strong" quake left his home "creaking and rattling".
"I was asleep when it hit. Everyone has run outside now and is too afraid to go back in. I'm currently driving to an open area to sleep in my car," he said.
Broadcaster CCTV also showed emergency personnel with helmets carrying a person and shining flashlights on damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs.
Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information.
'Significant casualties'
President Xi Jinping said the tremor caused "significant casualties" and took place at a "high-altitude location" in cold weather.
"(We) must go all-out to carry out search and rescue operations and do our utmost to treat the injured, so as to minimise casualties," Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.
He called for assistance for residents and rescue equipment to be sent to the area promptly.
The epicentre was in a mountainous area about 190km east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390km northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.
It struck at 10.33pm on Thursday at a shallow depth of around 10km.
Lhawang Dagpo, a local official in the Maru township, the quake's epicentre, said it put cracks in the walls of his office, according to Xinhua.
Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.
Baqing County has mobilised more than 1,600 people to help in the relief operation, CCTV reported.
"The municipal fire and rescue brigade has dispatched 25 vehicles and 110 personnel, and the Nagqu Armed Police Detachment sent 225 officers and soldiers and 18 vehicles," CCTV said.
"As of 4.30am on Thursday, relief supplies including 1,000 prefabricated houses, 3,239 tents, four generators and 1,000 flashlights had been delivered," it added.
Earthquakes in China are relatively common.
In January 2025, a quake in Tibet's rural Tingri county killed at least 126 people.
The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media.
That quake was China's deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan.
A massive tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left about 90,000 people dead or missing, including around thousands of schoolchildren.
3ad16c876a13b12b: Energy can be hard to find on Friday mornings, which is why The Register uses them to offer a fresh instalment of On Call – the reader-contributed column that shares your hopefully empowering tech support stories.

This week, meet a reader we’ll Regomize as “Lachlan,” who told us he once did tech support for a senior exec who had a side hustle writing essays for Japanese university students attending UK universities.
The exec asked Lachlan for help diagnosing a sudden inability to send or receive email, an obvious hindrance to the side hustle.
This story took place in the dialup age, so Lachlan sensibly assumed that the exec’s modem was misbehaving.
“I checked the network settings, nothing wrong there,” he told On Call. Next, he checked the cables, and if the line the modem used had a dial tone. Again, all was well.

“At this point I decided to make sure the device was correctly installed in Windows Device Manager,” Lachlan wrote. “I had a lot of experience in the dark arts of serial communications and there was an option in the advanced settings in Device Manager to send a series of low level AT commands to the modem, which would return responses.”
He ran the tests, and Windows reported that the modem was in the pink of health.
With all that done, Lachlan decided the time had come to replace the modem.

“When I opened the PC, I got a faint whiff of that unmistakable scorched PCB smell,” he wrote. “By looking at the modem you couldn’t normally see if any of the chips were faulty. In this case there was a black soot mark in the shape of the voltage regulator chip which sits between the phone line and the sensitive chips on the modem.”

“This was to protect the device from the 70V line voltage BT used to create a phone connection,” he explained. “However, in this instance the chip had been vaporized. That wasn’t just a slight over voltage – this was way higher.”
Lachlan asked the exec when his email had stopped working, and if he could recall any recent electrical storms.
He replied by saying his email stopped working while he watched a really impressive display of lightning.
“That voltage regulator chip sacrificed itself for the greater good,” Lachlan wrote.

Has Windows failed to find an obvious fault? Or has lightning lightened your load? In either case, click here to send your story to On Call so we can electrify your fellow readers on a future Friday. ®
b518cbbf44ace6cc: WELLINGTON: The head of New Zealand's military has resigned over an "inappropriate relationship" he had while in charge of a unit, the Defence Force said Friday.
"The resignation is for personal reasons, and results from errors of judgement made by me in the past, for which I am taking responsibility," Air Marshal Tony Davies said.
"The errors of judgement were contrary to the values of the Defence Force," he added.
"These matters revolved around an inappropriate relationship I had when in a position of unit command, and I regret not disclosing this when I had the opportunity to do so."
He asked for privacy and said that his focus was on his family at this time, the military added.
The matter has been referred to an independent oversight body, the military said.
New Zealand's defence minister Paul Goldsmith said the circumstances around the resignation would come as a "great disappointment" to many in the armed forces.
"The reasons regarding his decision relate to integrity matters, that he did not previously disclose," he said.
"We both agree his position is no longer tenable."
Approached for comment by AFP, the New Zealand Defence Force declined to offer further details.
Previously head of the air force, Davies was appointed chief of New Zealand's military in 2024.
a5ba3ee615181c3a: PETALING JAYA: Pemimpin Bersama Rafizi Ramli mahu menyaman R Ramanan berhubung dakwaan yang dilemparkan oleh naib presiden PKR itu terhadapnya dalam satu sidang media baru-baru ini.
Rafizi mendakwa, Ramanan yang juga menteri sumber manusia membuat pelbagai tuduhan terhadapnya, termasuk mengaitkannya dengan amalan rasuah.

"Saya telah berbincang dengan pasukan peguam saya dan mereka berpendapat ada asas kukuh untuk memulakan tindakan saman terhadap Ramanan, kerana kenyataan-kenyataan dalam sidang media itu telah melanggar garis-garis yang ditetapkan oleh undang-undang fitnah di negara ini.
"Oleh itu, saya telah mengarahkan peguam-peguam saya untuk memulakan proses saman terhadap Ramanan," katanya menerusi kenyataan hari ini.

Rafizi berkata, rakaman video serta transkrip sidang media itu telah diserahkan kepada peguamnya, sambil menegaskan tindakan undang-undang wajar diambil kerana Ramanan terus mengelak daripada menjawab beberapa dakwaan berkaitan rasuah.

"Jika Ramanan enggan mengambil tindakan saman terhadap saya, akibat dari sidang media beliau semalam, ia membuka jalan untuk saya mengheret beliau ke mahkamah susulan tohmahan-tohmahan yang dibuat terhadap saya," katanya.

Sebelum ini, Ramanan memberitahu pemberita pada majlis bersama warga kementeriannya bahawa beliau tidak akan menyaman Rafizi berhubung dakwaan bekas Ahli Parlimen Pandan itu dalam sebuah audio siar, kononnya seorang wakil rakyat PKR menerima RM9.5 juta untuk bertindak sebagai orang tengah dalam pertikaian membabitkan kumpulan mafia korporat.

Ramanan berkata, Rafizi sepatutnya membuat laporan kepada pihak berkuasa jika mempunyai bukti sahih. Tambahnya, saman hanya akan membebankan orang ramai jika Rafizi mengutip derma bagi menampung kos guamannya.
Pada majlis sama, Ramanan dilaporkan melabel Rafizi sebagai 'penipu bersiri' serta menyifatkan tumpuan bekas menteri itu terhadap isu lain sekadar taktik asas mengalih perhatian politik.

Beliau turut merujuk dakwaan pihak lain bahawa Rafizi pernah menerima rasuah RM500,000 berkaitan Datasonic, di samping siasatan Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) berhubung perjanjian kerajaan dengan Arm Holdings.
Pertikaian itu tercetus selepas Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menepis dakwaan Rafizi di Dewan Rakyat, setelah beberapa Ahli Parlimen membangkitkannya.
Walaupun Anwar selaku presiden PKR tidak menamakan Ahli Parlimen berkenaan, Ramanan sebelum ini menafikan tuduhan bahawa beliau wakil rakyat PKR yang dimaksudkan itu.
f24ab83723ec9c33: PETALING JAYA: A private dental practitioners’ group has raised concerns over the growing use of unethical and misleading advertising by dental clinics.
The Malaysian Private Dental Practitioners’ Association (MPDPA) said some dentists were using questionable marketing tactics and engaging third-party agencies to solicit patients.

"Heavily discounted treatment packages, unrealistic promotional offers and aggressive price-driven advertising raise serious concerns about whether patients are given complete and accurate information before making healthcare decisions," it said in a statement today.

The group said advertisements promoting exceptionally low fees might not disclose additional charges, treatment package limitations, material specifications or the full cost of completing a procedure.
Patients could be attracted by advertised prices, only to discover that the actual cost was considerably higher, it said.
Crucially, patients risked making treatment decisions based on promotions rather than clinical suitability, treatment quality and long-term outcomes, the association added.
MPDPA also questioned whether appropriate clinical standards could be consistently maintained when clinics compete primarily on price.
Dental procedures require suitable materials, proper sterilisation, sufficient clinical time, professional expertise and ongoing patient care, it said.
The group called for a review of the Malaysian Dental Council’s Guidelines and Provisions for Public Information, issued in July 2022, which cover dental clinics’ use of social media for advertising.

It urged the council to provide clearer and more practical guidance on online promotions, discounted treatment packages, pricing claims, patient testimonials, influencer collaborations and advertising by third-party marketing agencies.
"Clear examples of permitted and prohibited practices would help dental practitioners understand their obligations, reduce ambiguity and support consistent enforcement.

"Revised guidelines must keep pace with changing digital trends while upholding professional ethics, protecting patients from misleading claims and ensuring that commercial interests do not compromise public trust in dental care," it said.
74693b2d8f4cd7e3: SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — Police uncovered drug trafficking at an unregistered house of worship in Klang during operations across Selangor from Oct 13 to 19.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a local man who worked part-time as an assistant at the house of worship was detained to assist the investigation.

“A raid led to the discovery of 20.6 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin inside the storage room of the house of worship. Investigations are ongoing. We do not rule out that the premises were used to store drugs.
“Checks also revealed that the temple is unregistered and the land is gazetted as a site for sewerage,” he told a press conference at the Selangor Police Contingent Headquarters here today.

In separate raids in Rawang and at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), police arrested seven individuals, comprising two local men, a local woman, three foreign men and a foreign woman, Shazeli said.
He said the individuals, aged between 19 and 48, had no prior criminal records except one local man with seven previous offences.
He added that the operations seized 81.3 kg of cannabis buds, 37 kg of ganja, one bottle and 3,510 cartridges of ketamine, 84 bottles of ecstasy, and 25.4 kg of ketamine.

“The total value of the seized drugs is estimated at RM16.2 million. Police also confiscated two cars, a motorcycle, and local and foreign currencies totalling RM54,835,” he said, adding the case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
In a separate case, Shazeli said suspected theft is believed to be the motive behind the abuse of a foreign domestic helper, who suffered burn injuries on her body.
He said investigations found the victim had been working for her employer since late last year.
“Investigations are currently being completed. It is believed the incident occurred because the victim was suspected of stealing and damaging her employer’s property,” he said.
It was reported that three women were among five individuals remanded for four days to assist in the investigation. — Bernama
6970aa44f0fde1de: SINGAPORE, Oct 23 — Reuniting with loved ones during festive seasons is something many look forward to.
But for some, particularly those travelling to Ipoh, Malaysia for Chinese New Year (CNY) next year, it can come at a hefty price.
This comes as flight ticket prices surge during the holiday season, with low-cost carrier fares soaring to new heights.

A check by AsiaOne on Thursday (Oct 22) found that one-way Scoot flights from Singapore to Ipoh cost significantly more in the week leading up to CNY (January 30 to February 5, 2027) — at S$734.20 (RM2,347)
In comparison, flights on the same route ranged from S$105.20 to S$241.20 just days before (January 23 to 28), before bumping up to S$562.20 on January 29.
Meanwhile, flights from Ipoh to Singapore saw a similar trend, with ticket prices peaking on February 8, the third day of Chinese New Year, at S$686.45.

Prices remained elevated in the following days, before starting to fall from February 15 at S$596.45. Flights from Ipoh to Singapore for the rest of the month from February 16 ranged from S$48.45 to S$193.45.

This means a round trip during the festive season could set travellers back at least S$1,420 — if they want to make it to Ipoh in time for reunion dinner on February 5 and return a few days to a week after.
And that’s before factoring in any additional charges such as checked baggage and seat selection.
While it is common to see airfares surge during festive periods, this marks a new high, as Ipoh-Singapore round trip prices only reached around S$1,100 previously, according to Shin Min Daily News.
For reference, the cheapest return flight between Singapore and Ipoh on Scoot outside of the peak festive period in the same month is about S$153.65.
However, other flights to different parts of Malaysia appeared to cost significantly less.
A separate check by AsiaOne on the same day saw that the most expensive round trip from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur on Singapore Airlines, which Scoot is a subsidiary of, was S$812.
If travelling on Scoot, a return flight between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur cost at least S$914.65 during the peak period.
Currently, Scoot is the only airline with a direct route between Singapore and Ipoh.
The flight time is around an hour and 15 minutes.
Previously, AirAsia also offered direct flights between the two locations before it suspended the route in April 2025.
Batik Air subsequently started flying between Singapore and Ipoh directly in December 2025. However, it ended the service in May this year. — AsiaOne
18358038f956e248: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers have welcomed the repayment relief measures announced under Budget 2027, saying the deferment and lower monthly payments will help ease financial pressures, particularly among fresh graduates.

Under the measures, borrowers earning less than RM2,500 a month will be allowed to defer repayments, while those earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000 will only need to pay a minimum of RM50 a month. Borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments will also receive a 10 per cent discount.

For Jeremiah Abraham Selvaraj, 43, a cyber security consultant, the education loan was instrumental in helping him complete his bachelor’s degree in mechatronics engineering at Monash University Malaysia and improve his family’s socioeconomic circumstances.

“Without this financial assistance, it would have been impossible for me to complete my higher education. The loan has helped those from lower and middle-income families improve their living standards,” he said.
He described the new repayment measures, including the RM50 monthly minimum, as a considerate move that would help ease the financial burden on fresh graduates.
Jeremiah, who has maintained a consistent repayment record without arrears, also said the 10 per cent discount for regular repayments served as an incentive to maintain financial discipline.

Customer service officer Carol Chan, 24, who is also a PTPTN borrower, welcomed the repayment deferment for those earning less than RM2,500 a month, saying it would give fresh graduates more time to stabilise their finances as they entered the workforce.
“The initiative helps ease our financial burden as we establish ourselves in our careers, allowing us to stabilise our daily expenses and strengthen our finances first,” she said.
Meanwhile, marketing executive Fatin Yusoff, 36, viewed the 10 per cent discount for borrowers without arrears who make regular repayments as recognition of their commitment.
Having maintained her repayments consistently over the past four years, she said the incentive would encourage borrowers to remain disciplined in meeting their obligations.
“When there are incentives like this, it feels as though our efforts are appreciated. The savings from the discount can be channelled into an emergency fund or other essential expenses,” she said.

Hafizul Fiqri Mazlan, 41, a graphic designer at the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (FINAS) who fully repaid his PTPTN loan in 2019, said borrowers should make full use of the repayment incentives.

He said the deferment for borrowers earning less than RM2,500 a month and the RM50 minimum monthly repayment for those earning below RM3,000 would be particularly helpful to those who had just started working.

Hafizul, a former student of Kolej Antarabangsa Yayasan Melaka (KAYM), also welcomed the 10 per cent discount, noting that previously, he had only been able to obtain a discount by settling his loan in full.
He stressed that borrowers had a responsibility to repay their loans so that the funds could continue helping other students pursue higher education.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the repayment measures when tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9. — Bernama
a996333bb9f6ff0c: SINGAPORE: Singapore Exchange CEO Loh Boon Chye said on Friday that the bourse operator had begun planning for an eventual leadership transition, although no date had been set for his departure.
In a statement delivered at SGX's annual general meeting, Loh said he had recently informed the chairman that planning should begin for a future CEO transition.
Loh joined the bourse operator as chief executive officer in July 2015 and also serves as an executive and non-independent director on its board. His current contract runs until mid-July 2027.

The potential transition comes as SGX seeks to build on growth across its securities, derivatives and foreign exchange businesses, while Singapore pushes to reinvigorate its equities market and attract more listings.

Last year, the city-state introduced a 20% tax rebate for primary listings and established a framework for dual listings on the SGX and Nasdaq, as part of broader efforts to strengthen its capital markets.

bd306255c8b5209e: Our economy needs it. The NHS needs it. And making foreign workers’ lives more miserable – as the home secretary plans to do – will undermine integration My mum’s carer was uncharacteristically late one morning. She didn’t want to say why at first, but it turned out she’d found her previous client – an elderly lady living all alone, with no family to visit – collapsed on the floor, barely alive. It was a lot to cope with for someone only in their early 20s, a reminder of the heavy responsibility this job carries. Watching the carers who helped both my parents in their respective final weeks taught me that while the work itself might seem mundane, the emotional and social skills needed to do it well – to coax some sense out of the confused, to jolly along the lonely, and to soothe the dying, to walk in and out of unfamiliar houses all day long without quite knowing what you might find – are anything but. Yet like so many jobs predominantly done by women, care has long been relentlessly undervalued. That means lousy pay, little public recognition, and now – at least for the disproportionately large chunk of this workforce who are migrant workers – the disorientating realisation that the government can snap its fingers and all your life plans are upended overnight. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

ea6f248a80ac0efd: PUTRAJAYA: Four Sarawak natives failed in their bid to claim RM51.76 million in damages over 474ha of disputed land in Saratok, despite the Court of Appeal ruling that the High Court had wrongly declined to hear their case.
In the main judgment, Justice Evrol Mariette Peters said the claimants failed to prove their native customary rights (NCR) over the land at Sungai Geruyu, also known as Sungai Ruyu.
A three-member panel chaired by Justice Wong Kian Kheong, sitting with Justice Alwi Abdul Wahab and Peters, unanimously dismissed the appeal.
Peters said the claimants did not establish, on a balance of probabilities, that they had occupied, cultivated or settled on the land in accordance with customary practices before Jan 1, 1958.
Their oral evidence was vague, while the maps produced were insufficiently reliable to establish the location and boundaries of the land in question, she said.
Peters also held that the title held by THP Saribas Sdn Bhd remained protected under the Sarawak Land Code.
"The claim was additionally time-barred, as the alleged trespass was discovered in 2005 but proceedings were only initiated in 2017," she said.
The appellants were Edward Gella Baul, Desmond Reynold Jemeni, Katol Anak Tutom, also known as Tatol, and Lengkong Anak Aba, who sued on behalf of themselves and 20 other claimants.
In a supporting judgment, Wong agreed with Peters but elaborated on why the High Court had jurisdiction.
He said Section 5(3)(a)(i) of the Native Courts Ordinance 1992 requires disputes over NCR land to be first heard by the district native court only when they are between natives.
Wong said the provision could not apply because THP Saribas was a company and not a native under the legislation.
He concluded that "the district native court had no jurisdiction to decide the dispute regarding the land, Lot 21", adding that the High Court was the right forum to hear the case.
Wong also distinguished earlier court decisions involving disputes between natives over customary land.
Despite the findings on jurisdiction, the appeal was dismissed with costs because the claimants failed to establish their substantive land claim.

f132cb2703901e83: TAIPEI, Oct 23 — Most shops and schools were shut across Taiwan on Friday as Typhoon Champi neared the island, forcing hundreds of people to leave their homes ahead of the powerful storm.
The typhoon is expected to sweep past Taiwan’s northeast as it moves towards China and Japan, triggering the cancellation of hundreds of flights in the region.
At least one person has been killed in Taiwan after being swept away by waves whipped up by the typhoon, authorities said. Dozens of others have been injured.
Champi is the latest in a busy Pacific storm season turbo-charged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.

The storm was briefly a super typhoon as it crossed the ocean, but has since weakened and is now packing maximum sustained wind speeds of 176 kilometres (109 miles) per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Centre.
Heavy rain, strong winds and giant waves are forecast for Friday and Saturday, and thousands of military personnel are on standby to assist with rescue efforts.
More than 1,200 people had been evacuated from their homes ahead of Champi.
“As it approaches Taiwan’s northeastern tip... the typhoon may slow down. If it slows down, its impact will last longer,” Central Weather Administration administrator Lu Kuo-chen told a briefing.
Champi is expected to dump up to 90 centimetres (35 inches) of rain from Thursday to Saturday, with northeastern Taiwan to be hardest hit, the forecaster said.
“People should be aware that the strong winds and extremely heavy rain will continue into the first half of tomorrow,” Lu added.
Work and classes were cancelled for the day across nearly all of Taiwan, leaving streets quiet as most locals hunkered down at home to wait out the storm.
Some businesses installed sandbags or metal barriers at entrances to prevent flooding of their premises.
“I’m worried about flooding. The vegetables could get flooded and rot, a 73-year-old farmer surnamed Tsai told AFP in New Taipei City.
Convenience store worker Peter Chen said he was concerned about the weather conditions on Friday night when the eye of the typhoon would be closer to Taiwan’s coast.
“We might prepare some sandbags,” the 27-year-old said.
The United Nations said Wednesday that the El Nino system gripping the planet is heading off the charts, and that countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is expected to peak in December, but the human impact is set to last into 2027 and beyond.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate human-caused global warming. — AFP

5c3561ea9e200969: PETALING JAYA: Pengerusi Biro Undang-Undang DAP Ramkarpal Singh menyeru Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail memberi penjelasan sama ada polis akan meneruskan siasatan terhadap tiga peguam mewakili keluarga Noorizwan Zulkefly, yang meninggal dunia dalam tahanan, awal bulan ini.

262d91e83cab93ea: LONDON, Oct 23 — A huge trove of Horatio Nelson’s letters, in which the British naval commander fantasises about his lover, Emma Hamilton, plans battles and scrawls after losing an arm, is expected to fetch millions at auction in London.

The pre-eminent vice-admiral, who achieved victories against revolutionary France and Napoleon but was killed in the Battle of Trafalgar, was a prolific letter writer despite losing an arm and part of his vision in battles.

A British businessman who admired him, Clive Richards, spent decades collecting some 400 letters and other historic documents now on sale at Sotheby’s with an estimate of £4 million to £6 million (US$5.3 million to US$8 million, RM22 million to RM33 million).

“It’s an absolutely astonishing collection and I think what really distinguishes it is that it captures every aspect of Nelson’s life and career,” said Sotheby’s books and manuscripts specialist Gabriel Heaton.
Scandalously, Nelson lived openly with his lover, society beauty Hamilton, though both were married, and their letters make clear their devotion.
By contrast, a message to his wife says he is too busy to write often.
Hamilton kept Nelson’s love letters, many on display at Sotheby’s until the closing date for bids on November 18.

In one written at sea in 1800, Nelson says: “last night I did nothing but dream of you”, recounting how she embraced him and whispered “I love nothing but you my Nelson”, after which he kissed her “fervently” and “we enjoy’d the height of love”.
This letter was sold by Christie’s in 2003 for nearly £120,000 (RM658,800).
After a victory in Copenhagen in 1801, soon after Emma gave birth to his child, Nelson wrote he was “very tired after a hard fought Battle” — but still managed to compose a short love poem.

Nelson had to learn to write with his left hand after his right arm was shattered by a musket in 1797; in one letter soon after the injury, he apologises before the words tail off and his wife takes over.
“You can see he’s struggling. You know, he’s actually forming the letters quite clearly, but it’s hard, hard work,” Heaton told AFP.
Subsequent letters show Nelson’s penmanship stayed messier than before, while emphatic with frequent underlinings.
The collection includes Nelson’s signature on battle plans for Trafalgar.
Nelson burnt Hamilton’s letters and only two are known to exist — both acquired by Richards.
In one dashed down rapidly, Hamilton writes in October 1805: “how do I idolise you my dearest Husband of my Heart you are all in this world to your Emma” and appeals “may god preserve you”.
But this letter only reached Nelson after his death, hit by a bullet on the deck of his ship HMS Victory.
Sadly, Hamilton’s last letters beg friends for financial support: she spent time in a debtors’ prison before fleeing to France where she died in 1815. — AFP

8fcfb24b54054503: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The age classification for films rated 18 is not a licence to screen content without restrictions, as such films remain subject to the screening guidelines in force.

The Communications Ministry stressed that the Film Censorship Board (LPF) under the Home Ministry would continue to assess film content based on aspects of public safety and order, religion, sociocultural matters, as well as decency and morality.

"Content that violates the screening guidelines, including material that could undermine social harmony, remains subject to appropriate action,” the ministry said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.

The reply was in response to a question from Datuk Ahmad Saad (PN-Pokok Sena), who asked for the ministry’s position on the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia’s (FINAS) move to stop cutting scenes from films rated PG18 in the name of openness.

The ministry said allowing 18-rated films to be screened without the removal of certain scenes represented a shift from controlling content through scene cuts to regulating access through age-based classification, rather than a relaxation of content restrictions.
It said that under this approach, films meeting the requirements could be screened without certain scenes being cut, but would be subject to strict age classification.

"The 2024 Film Censorship Guidelines detail classification categories based on viewers’ age suitability, which, among other things, enable adults to make informed choices about the films they wish to watch.

"They are also intended to educate and protect teenagers and children from exposure to content that is inappropriate for their age and could affect their behaviour, while placing responsibility on parents to monitor and guide their children in choosing suitable content,” the ministry said.

It added that FINAS and LPF would continue to work with industry players to review the film classification system to ensure it remained relevant to industry developments and the current content landscape.

Meanwhile, the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), established following the enforcement of the Malaysian Media Council Act 2025 (Act 868), plays a role in strengthening public media literacy in addressing the spread of false information, hate speech and the challenges posed by digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

The Communications Ministry said the council is also responsible for promoting the production of authentic, accurate and ethical media reports and content, strengthening compliance with journalistic codes of ethics, and providing transparent and effective public complaints mechanisms.

"To support the establishment and operation of the MMM, the government has provided legal support through the creation of a dedicated legal framework, as well as initial assistance for infrastructure development and administrative matters.

"Cooperation with relevant agencies also supports capacity-building and the professional development of media practitioners, including through training and the promotion of journalistic ethics,” it said in response to a question from Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) on the implementation status of Act 868 and the MMM, including its functions and responsibilities and the forms of government support provided. — Bernama

690aea53d2bd1733: Generative artificial intelligence models are rooted in ideas of mid-20th century engineers who thought some amount of irrationality was essential for a machine that could think like a human, contends Benjamin Lindquist, an assistant professor in the MIT History Section, who holds an MIT Schwarzman College of Computing shared position with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and is a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems.  To mimic creative thinking, these AI pioneers intentionally injected randomness into algorithms designed to deterministically solve problems, Lindquist writes in a new paper that appears in the journal Past and Present. In the paper, he traces the origins of AI hallucinations back to this early research and suggests there will be inevitable tradeoffs between creativity and predictability when trying to build machines that mimic human behavior. MIT News spoke with Lindquist about these ideas. Q: Why did early computer engineers believe they needed to inject randomness and irrationality into AI systems designed for logic and calculation?  A: There is a long history of many figures in the world of science and art theorizing that chance plays an important part in discovery and creativity — in the ability to originate ideas. They equated creativity with unexpected leaps of logic, or even a dream-like state that allows you to think about things from a new perspective.  In the early 1950s, one popular idea from John Pierce, who was a prominent electrical engineer at Bell Labs, was about math being valuable in the world of art. The idea was shared by a lot of people working in early computing. When we think of artwork that includes math, we may think of something very orderly and precise, but Pierce came to the opposite conclusion. He concluded that the utility of math is that it could remove order from art. Then in a very calculated way, math could add a burst of the unexpected as a means to deviate from clichés and add an element of irregularity which just might lead to insight.  One popular way to add irregularity into otherwise predictable computers was through artificial (or random) neural networks. Many early neural networks were built by psychologists, who thought that by enabling scientists to build a model of the brain, artificial neural networks allowed scientists to observe what is happening inside, including how brains make productive mistakes. Rather than being black boxes, researchers believed these systems could open this black box of the mind and let scientists peer inside and see all the messy stuff that was really happening. But there was another camp in the world of AI who thought that creative thinking was just “normal” thinking done better. It is interesting to look at these two very simplistic heuristics for understanding intelligence and creativity, and how they do and don’t mesh. The debate, then, was about trying to determine what human inventiveness boils down to, and then how to reconstitute human inventiveness in machine form.  Q: How did these early computer engineers view AI, and how is it different from the way we think about AI today? A: When we think of AI systems, we think of ChatGPT or Claude. We value and use these systems because they give answers that, most of the time, are correct. One of the things that was most interesting to me in this research was finding out that a lot of the early advocates of these systems valued them for exactly the opposite reason. They wanted a system that, on occasion, gave answers that deviated from their expectations. They already had systems that could deliver reasonable and expected answers. They saw neural networks as valuable because they could give unexpected, perhaps even strange and bizarre answers. One reason we might view these systems differently today could be because of how they operate. Early on, these systems were confined to laboratories, so there weren’t really any real-world consequences of a system that gives a strange, or wrong, output. But now there are legal and monetary reasons why OpenAI or Anthropic doesn’t want a chatbot that gives unexpected or creative answers. There has been a “sanding down” of strangeness in these systems. They still potentially have that at their core, but it is something that is now largely suppressed. Q: How did early neural networks that incorporated randomness to simulate human creativity evolve to become the dominant paradigm in AI? A: For a long time, a specific kind of AI called “symbolic AI” was the dominant approach. Essentially, symbolic AI says the world is based on rules. The role of the AI researcher is to try and reconstruct the knowledge of the world in facts and propositions and feed it into a computer. Neural networks, with their use of randomness to solve problems, started to gain traction in the 1950s but fell out favor early on. Frank Rosenblatt, a psychologist who was a very important early figure in neural networks, died prematurely; he died accidentally on his 43rd birthday in 1971. He was quite a charismatic and forceful personality, who made a lot of grand promises about what systems based on neural networks could do. By the time he died, a shift toward symbolic AI was already underway. It is possible if, had he lived, things might have turned out differently. But neural networks never went away. By the 1980s they had shifted more into the world of cognitive science. To become more powerful, and more useful, neural networks needed a lot of data and computational power. That didn’t really arrive until the advent of the internet, when a lot of data became available and computing started to power up. Around 2012, neural networks started to outperform and outpace a statistical form of machine learning, and they kept growing from there. Q: What lessons can we learn from studying AI’s history that could inform its development?  A: I think there is a cautionary lesson here. The ideas and experiences of these early engineers tell us that we can work toward quashing hallucinations — we can work toward making AI perform a certain way so it doesn’t produce unexpected or unwanted answers — but there are going to be other consequences of that. These historical figures were onto something. There is a connection between the surprising and creative conclusions AI can offer and errors or hallucinations. There are tradeoffs when we build our systems to behave one way or the other. Maybe it is impossible to be completely at either end of the spectrum, but when we work toward one thing robustly, we often sacrifice something else unintentionally.

291f0719d1e3f06f: "Malaysians asked to remove haze, government asking to remove Waze". Satu lagi berbunyi, "ask government to settle haze, they got rid of Waze". Tak tahu siapa yang mencipta ungkapan itu tetapi dia memang creative buat lawak sinis.

Ada rhyme 'haze' dengan 'Waze'. Kata-kata itu sudah mendapat tempat di pelbagai platform media sosial. Saya sendiri tersenyum lebar membacanya. Ini susulan tindakan kerajaan melarang penjawat awam menggunakan aplikasi navigasi Waze berkuat kuasa serta-merta. Walaupun larangan membabitkan hanya kakitangan kerajaan, orang ramai turut digalakkan berhenti guna Waze.
Oleh kerana jerebu masih bersama kita, terciptalah jenaka sinis 'haze' dan 'waze' yang disebut tadi. Namun jika diambil kira alasan kerajaan, this is no laughing matter.

Kata Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, tindakan diambil bagi melindungi maklumat kerajaan dan data peribadi pengguna yakni penjawat awam daripada ancaman penyalahgunaan oleh rejim Israel. Keputusan dibuat PMX dengan mengambil kira kedudukan Waze Mobile Ltd sebagai pengawal data pengguna yang diperbadankan dan beroperasi di bawah undang-undang Israel.

Berkata pula Menteri Digital Gobind Singh Deo, "jika melihat dokumen perjanjian (sebelum mengaktifkan aplikasi) kita bersetuju dengan syarat-syarat tertentu iaitu di bawah bidang kuasa undang-undang Israel dan itu menjadi satu masalah kepada kita."

Majlis Keselamatan Negara pula kata tiada kompromi terhadap sebarang risiko keselamatan melibatkan Israel. Reaksi Waze ialah menafikan aplikasinya mengumpulkan maklumat sensitif kerajaan atau membenarkan pihak ketiga mengeksplotasi data peribadi pengguna. Penafian ini memang dijangkakan.
Larangan kerajaan stands. Ketua Pengarah MKN Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin berkata penjawat awam yang melanggar arahan boleh dikenakan tindakan tatatertib.

Saya percaya ramai dalam kalangan ribuan penjawat awam menggunakan Waze. Yang membingungkan saya bagaimana mahu memastikan semua yang menggunakan Waze mematuhi arahan. Adakah setiap penjawat awam akan diperiksa seorang demi seorang? Mengambil kira bilangan kakitangan awam yang guna Waze, pelaksanaan arahan tentunya bukan mudah.
Kata MKN, "dari segi pelaksanaan arahan ada caranya tetapi secara umum kita serahkan kepada ketua jabatan masing-masing". That is not saying much.
Oleh kerana jutaan rakyat menggunakan Waze tentunya larangan kerajaan menarik perhatian ramai.

Pertanyaan ramai ialah why now? Mungkinkah berdasarkan informasi terkini? Jika penggunaan Waze mengancam keselamatan negara dan diri sendri apa lagi yang mengancam ialah Israel, mengapa larangan tidak menyeluruh dan membabitkan semua rakyat, meskipun saya akui ini akan menyebabkan kesulitan.

Menurut Raja Nushirwan, kerajaan mengambil pendekatan berfasa berteraskan pendidikan awam demi mengimbangi tuntutan keselamatan dan kebebasan memilih rakyat. Maka sekarang eloklah kita tunggu 'pendidikan awam' yang beliau katakan. Dalam bentuk apa agaknya ia akan disalurkan kepada rakyat?
"Dengan cara yang kita ambil ini kita serahkan kepada rakyat Malaysia untuk memilih secara sendiri," kata beliau. Terima kasih. Rakyat lain ada pilihan sendiri, tidak seperti penjawat awam.

Menurut Anwar, kerajaan menggalakkan orang ramai untuk menggunakan aplikasi tempatan, TuJu, yang dibangunkan oleh Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia sebagai alternatif bagi keperluan navigasi jalan raya. Jujur saya kata saya tidak tahu akan kewujudan TuJu. Pun begitu semasa menonton Buletin Utama tiga malam lalu, beberapa warganegara yang sudah lama menggunakan TuJu rata-rata puas hati dengan prestasi aplikasi itu.
Apabila Anwar mencadangkan orang ramai guna TuJu, ramai menyambut saranan beliau. Ada lonjakan ketara jumlah pengguna TuJu selepas PMX mengesyorkan pengunaannya. That’s on the upside.

On the downside tercetus gangguan teknikal yang menjejaskan perisian navigasi TuJu. Kata Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia ia sudah bekerjasama dengan penyedia aplikasi, Prosignal Consortium, untuk mengenal pasti punca gangguan, memulihkan kestabilan sistem serta meningkatkan kapasiti aplikasi bagi menampung jumlah pengguna yang semakin bertambah.

Bercakap mengenai penyedia aplikasi TuJu, macam-macam spekulasi dalam kalangan orang ramai yang saya tidak cadang menghuraikan, sekadar menyatakan memang biasa apabila kerajaan recommend sesuatu perkara, syarikat yang mengendalikannya akan diletak di bawah mikroskop. Kadangkala ada spekulasi betul dan ada yang bohong.

Apapun if there's anything good to come out of this Waze issue, it is proof that Malaysia atau lebih tepat rakyat boleh mencipta aplikasi membanggakan. Jika tidak lebih baik, ia setanding Waze. Semakin ramai kenal TuJu maka cepatlah atasi kesulitan.
